Those who achieve this gain the letters of the oldest language.
THE Primordial Source itself lies beyond even this.
It is not attained.
It is either carried from birth or approached through adversity so extreme that most existences collapse long before proximity becomes relevant.|
|This place is simultaneously the most dangerous and the most accelerating environment for Source development in existence.|
|Welcome.|
BOOM!
Noah blinked.

His Infinity rearranged itself around his Source with the specific efficiency of a system reconfiguring to new operational parameters, the multicolored currents cycling through him in patterns adapted to this place rather than the patterns that had served him in Observable Existence.
He felt the difference immediately.

The sensory fullness was extraordinary- the sand under his feet, the cold of the air, the smell of the dark water behind them, all of it arriving at an intensity that his cultivated existence had been filtering for so long that he had forgotten the unfiltered version existed.
He also felt hungry.
Not the cultivated awareness of needing to replenish reserves.
Actual hunger, the raw biological version that he had last felt when he was a young man eating whatever the apocalypse left available.
It pressed against his concentration with the insistence of a condition that had been waiting a very long time to be acknowledged.
A status panel bloomed at the edge of his perception.
|Source Status — Noah Osmont|
|Designations: THE Genesis Monarch / THE Youngest / THE Primus Apeiron / THE Infinite Speaker / THE Osmontian|
|Source: Emergent — Elevating /Galdr Source|
|Infinity: Nearu Absolute /Galdr|
|Observable Force: Galdr|
|Cause Links Active: THE Bellum Cause / THE Cognitio Cause / THE Infinite Cause|
|THE Infinite Tongue: Active at Source level|
|Satiety: 27%|
|Warning: Your Infinity expression at this Demarcation produces Source sapping at an accelerated rate relative to most Second Demarcation existences.
Your Source requires significantly greater replenishment volume than others at equivalent standing.
Consumption must commence soon.
At 10% Satiety, self-consumption begins.|
Noah looked at the 27% and looked at the warning and looked at the dark landscape stretching beyond the mile his perception could reach.
He pulled Adelheid upright from the jagged sand.

She was catching her breath, her golden Source expression cycling through the visible emotions this place amplified straight to the surface- residual fear from the crossing, the disorientation of having her Ubergulden identity stripped back to its raw core, the specific vulnerability of a being who had spent eons constructing an exterior discovering that the exterior was not present anymore.
He checked her status without asking.
Her Source was First Demarcation, stable but thin, her Satiety already higher than his at 70%.
He looked behind them at the obsidian waters.
He looked at the distant crimson eyes of the Source Eel still watching from the border of the void it had created.
He looked at the dark landscape ahead where anything from eons past or eons future might be waiting in the mile beyond his perception.

Twenty-seven percent Hunger and falling, in a place where the only replenishment was consuming something else’s Source or resources, in a space without time where a Fourth Scale creature had been the welcome party.
He had arrived at a truly glorious place!

chapters.title: Chapter 5246: Survival! I
paragraphs: Noah waved his hand.
Multicolored Infinity bloomed outward from his palm like a fire, illuminating the immediate surroundings with the warm cycling light of his Source expression. He looked at himself in the glow of it.

His fair skin glistened in the Infinity-light, every surface of him vivid in a way that cultivation had been quietly suppressing for so long he had forgotten this was what skin looked like when nothing was filtering it. His shoulders and abdomen were pronounced, the muscular definition of his frame rendered in sharp relief by the light, and across his front and behind, broad green leaves covered what they covered with the patient indifference of an environment that did not concern itself with modesty but had provided the minimum available.
He looked like something carved from a grand idea about what a man should look like.
He turned to check on Adelheid.
"Damn."

He said it before he could arrange his face around not saying it. He fully attributed it to the place amplifying every basal emotion to its unfiltered intensity, which was a factually accurate attribution, and which also did nothing to change the fact that the damn had been entirely warranted.

Ubergulden Adelheid’s fair gold skin shone dimly in his Infinity-light with the specific luminescence of a Source expression that was warm and genuine underneath every layer of engineering she had accumulated across her eons. Her figure was pronounced in the way that this place pronounced everything it stripped back to its essentials, and the broad leaves covering her chest and waist were providing coverage in the technical sense of the word.
She had not noticed him looking.
Because she was looking at him.

Her eyes moved across his figure with the specific unhurried assessment of a being whose basal emotions were also running at full unfiltered volume, her gold eyes tracking across his shoulders and abdomen and back up again with an expression she had not yet arranged into the composed neutrality she used for most situations.
They were both acclimating!

Then Noah’s Infinity pressed against something in the dark behind them and rang out a warning, and he grabbed Adelheid without deliberating and pulled her hard to the right as her warm figure pressed against him and they hit the ground rolling.
BOOM!

The ground where they had been standing exploded upward in a shower of dark sand and jagged rock, the impact deep enough to suggest the thing that had caused it was not small. When the debris settled, the creature stood in the crater it had made.

Twice their height. Obsidian from its snout to the blunt end of its abbreviated tail, its body low and wide and built in the way that things built for pure damage tended to be built, with no wasted space between its thick haunches and its broader shoulders. The fur, if it could be called fur, was dense obsidian-dark with the texture of compressed Source material rather than ordinary animal coat, each strand carrying a faint crimson luminescence that matched the blaze of its eyes. Its claws were longer than Noah’s forearm, the ends catching the Infinity-light and holding it in the way that things built for tearing held light.
A Honey Badger!

The obsidian honey badger looked at them with the crimson eyes of something that had been hunting in THE Source Lands for longer than it was comfortable to estimate and had not done so unsuccessfully.
A Seidr Source. First Demarcation.
It felt like considerably more than First Demarcation should feel.
That was the first thing Noah registered as the honey badger charged!
WUUU!

It moved low and fast and without any of the telegraphing that combat experience produced in beings who had fought other combat-experienced beings. It had not developed fighting instincts against opponents who could read its preparation. It had developed fighting instincts against everything in THE Source Lands, which meant it assumed nothing could read its preparation and moved accordingly.

Noah pushed Adelheid left and went right and the honey badger drove between them, its momentum carrying it past their positions before it arrested with a pivot that something its size had no business executing at that speed. It turned on Adelheid.
She was already moving.

Her Seidr Source flared gold around her as she drove her hands outward in the form of an attack that would have carried Paleozoic Scale Gilded authority in Observable Existence. Here it carried her Source expression raw, unstructured, pure gold light hammering into the honey badger’s flank as it turned toward her.
The honey badger absorbed it.

Not resisted. Absorbed, its obsidian coat pulling the Source energy inward in the way that things designed by long survival in this environment pulled available energy inward, and the honey badger’s crimson eyes burned fractionally brighter after the contact than before.
It was eating her attack!
WAP!

A claw caught Adelheid across the shoulder before Noah could close the distance and she spun backward hard, hitting the jagged rock of the beach with a sound that carried impact. She was upright before he reached her, her expression carrying the specific set of a being who had just received information about the gap between expectation and reality and was processing it at speed.
It felt like something that was Ordovician and Silurian at the same time!
"Hey." Noah stepped between her and the honey badger. "Stay close, okay?"
The honey badger regarded him.

He was a Galdr Source. It was a Seidr Source. By the Demarcation logic, the fight should have been straightforward. The honey badger’s crimson eyes calculated the multicolored light of his Source expression with the unhurried attention of something that had consumed Galdr Sources before and had survived the consumption, which told him the Demarcation advantage was real but not determinative against something that had spent eons learning exactly how to neutralize it.
He reached outward through THE Infinite Tongue. He controlled Infinity nearby!

The obsidian rivers running through the beach terrain responded. He pulled from them, gathering the obsidian Infinity they carried toward his grip, the material condensing under the Tongue’s direction into a shape that was not natural to it but that the Tongue imposed with the same ease it imposed any instruction. A spear. Dense, obsidian, burning faintly with his multicolored Infinity threaded through its core, the head carrying a compressed point that the material held because he had told it to!
The honey badger charged again.
Noah sidestepped and drove the spear at its flank rather than meeting it head-on, the point finding the gap between two dense obsidian fur clusters and going through. The honey badger screamed!
It was not a sound he had expected, genuine and harsh. and pivoted with the spear still in it, swinging its mass to use the weapon as a lever.
He released the spear before it pulled him off balance.

The honey badger turned back with the spear buried in its side and its eyes blazing, and charged again, and this time Adelheid came in from its opposite side with her Source expression driving downward onto its hindquarters, pulling its attention for the half-second Noah needed.
He reformed the spear from the obsidian in the ground beneath the honey badger.

It came up through the beach from below, the point driving through the underside of the creature’s jaw and continuing upward, and the honey badger’s charge became a stumble and the stumble became stillness, the obsidian body collapsing onto the dark sand with the finality of something very large ceasing all at once.
Silence!
Then the honey badger’s body began to glow.

Not dimly. The crimson of its eyes bled outward through its obsidian coat in slow waves, the Source energy it had carried across however many eons it had spent in THE Source Lands radiating outward from the cooling body in the way that concentrated energy radiated from things that had been containing it and were no longer containing it.
Noah’s Source burned.

It was the only word for it. The hunger pulled at his attention with the specific urgency of something biological that had been told there was food nearby and had no interest in polite deferral. He had not felt this feeling since the early apocalypse years and his Source was making extremely clear it intended to be fed!
|Combat concluded. Seidr Source: Honey Badger of THE Source Lands.|

|Source consumed: Seidr Grade. Racial capability noted- Absorption Hide: passive absorption of incoming Source expressions, converting external Source energy into the creature’s own reserves. All attacks backed by Source energy feed this capability. Physical strikes and expressions not backed by Source energy bypass the absorption.|

|Your Source expression absorbed during the engagement: minor. The Absorption Hide required the creature to be struck by Source-backed attacks repeatedly to accumulate significant reserves. You adapted before critical depletion.|

|Satiety recovery available: consuming this Source will restore approximately 80% Satiety for a standard Second Demarcation entity. Due to your accelerated depletion rate, this will restore approximately 40% of your Satiety.|
|Note: Your current Satiety stands at 23%. This recovery is insufficient for sustained operation. Continued hunting is required.|
Noah looked at the glowing body and at the 23% on his panel and at the dark landscape extending beyond his one-mile perception limit.

Adelheid was pressing her hand to the claw mark on her shoulder, the gold of her Source expression fluctuating at the site of the injury in the way of a wound that was processing the implications of being real rather than cultivated.
He looked at her.
"I will eat first..." he said. "Then we move and understand this place some more!"
WAA!
He crouched beside the honey badger’s Source-lit body, and his multicolored Infinity reached into it, and THE Source Lands’ most fundamental transaction commenced!

chapters.title: Chapter 5247: Survival! II
paragraphs: Ubergulden Dietrich arrived on the obsidian beach without his right hand.

The stump ended cleanly at the wrist, the Source energy at the terminus cycling through the slow regenerative process that a Seidr Source performed under catastrophic injury, which was to say it worked, and it worked at the pace of something working against odds that had not been calculated in advance.

Blood, real and warm and crimson-gold, dripped from the stump into the dark sand. He had forgotten blood could do that! His power had been filtering that particular detail for so long the forgetting had been complete.

Beside him, his Sororis Prima Custodes had arrived with the left half of her torso present and the right half reconstructing itself from what her Source could provide, the process producing visible results and visible cost simultaneously. She was on her knees in the dark sand, both hands flat on the ground for stability, her expression set with the rigid concentration of a being whose primary cognitive resource was entirely committed to not losing the regeneration’s progress.

Dietrich knelt beside her and pushed his own Source expression toward her, the gold of it pressing against the injury site with the intent of a Custos bond trying to do what Custodes bonds existed to do.
It was slow.

Seidr Sources under critical injury regenerated slowly. He knew this now in the empirical sense of having observed it across the last several minutes, which was more immediate knowledge than the theoretical understanding he had arrived with.
He pressed harder, but at such a time..
BOOM!

The impact came from his left and slightly above, the force carrying the specific signature of something that had been moving invisibly and had decided the moment for invisibility was done. Dietrich’s hand came up and caught the incoming mass, his Source expression flaring gold around the contact point, and something struck his palm hard enough to drive him two feet sideways across the dark sand!
He held.

Where he had caught it, the invisible thing became visible on contact with his Source, the crystalline exterior revealing itself as the expression that had been concealing it failed against the direct energy contact. It was a bullet ant, enormous, its body the length of his forearm with a crystalline carapace that caught the faint ambient light of the beach and scattered it in all directions, its Source energy blazing Seidr-bright as it gathered the surrounding obsidian Infinity and drove it outward in a focused stream toward his chest.

The obsidian Infinity hit him and he felt it differently than he had felt anything in Observable Existence, the impact not on his Civilization but on his Source directly, the raw core of what he was taking damage rather than the architectural layers built around it!
WUU!

He smashed his remaining hand into the ant’s carapace and heard the crack of crystalline material giving way under the force of his Source expression, and the ant disengaged and skittered backward across the rock, gathering more obsidian Infinity from the surrounding terrain for its next impact.
He looked at his Custodes, still on her hands and knees in the sand, still reconstructing.
He looked at the ant circling for its next approach.

He moved toward the ant and away from his Custos and felt the specific cold of that movement, leaving her exposed while he addressed what was coming for both of them, making the calculation that a slower threat to her was preferable to an immediate one arriving at her back while he remained where he was.
The ant came at him, and he met it, and behind him his Custos continued her slow reconstruction in the dark.
This place was very dangerous!
Elsewhere.
Arjunstood on the body of the giant Seidr Crab and ate.

The crab’s carapace had been split across its dorsal surface from the force of whatever had ended it, the interior meat exposed and glowing faintly with the residual Source energy the creature had carried. He ate without ceremony, tearing pieces away with his hands and consuming them with the focused efficiency of a being who had identified this as the primary task and was executing it.

His muscular frame gleamed faintly in the ambient dark, the leaves covering his lower body the only concession to the environment’s preference for basic coverage. He was broad across the shoulders and composed in every line of his bearing, the imperious gold-blue of his Source expression radiating outward from him in a steady ambient glow that the darkness of this place did not quite manage to suppress.

Even stripped to his Source, stripped of every layer of Superbius engineering and Royal House identity, Arjun carried himself as something that had never received information about what peers looked like.

His Custodes sat at the edge of the crab’s carapace, breathing heavily. The crossing had cost her and the first engagement after had cost her further, and she was eating her portion of the crab with the focused intent of someone restoring themselves against a deficit that was not comfortable to be carrying.
Arjun chewed and looked at the dark landscape ahead.
"We will delve deeper while killing and eating everything in our path."
He said this between bites without turning his head, as though he were narrating a plan he had already fully formed and was now simply communicating for the benefit of whoever was present.

"The creatures here are dangerous. They are steeped in the power of this place in ways that cultivated strength does not fully account for. Even a Silurian Paleozoic entity can fall to them if they are not careful." He tore another piece free and ate.
"What matters is one’s Source. Infinity is a large factor. So are others. Seidr is one stage, and we have to reach Galdr Source quickly. Then we will have the confidence to go truly deeper."
He looked at the dark horizon where the one-mile perception limit cut off his view.

"Galdr is the stage, and we will be the first ones to reach it." He paused on this, not out of uncertainty but with the patience of someone giving a statement the weight it deserved. "Looking at the dangers of this place, the monstrous creatures and the ambient pressure, that poor sister of Dietrich’s will likely die soon if she has not already."
He consumed the last piece he had taken and stood upright on the crab’s body, looking ahead.
"If we meet her, I will be magnanimous enough to offer her shelter. In the end, even across separate Houses, we all seek the same glory."
His eyes carried the bright imperious light of a being who had stripped every external layer away and found that what remained was entirely comfortable with what it was.
"The glory of Gilded Ones."
His Custodes finished her portion and stood beside him, her breathing steadied, her Source expression cycling back toward functional.
Arjun looked at the dark landscape with the expression of a being who had located the horizon and found it his for the taking!

He stepped off the crab’s body and moved into the dark, and his Custodes followed, and behind them the crab’s slowly dimming Source remained on the dark sand like a marker of where something had ended so that something else could continue.

"Galdr is the stage, and we will be the first ones to reach it." He paused on this, not out of uncertainty but with the patience of someone giving a statement the weight it deserved.
"Looking at the dangers of this place, the monstrous creatures and the ambient pressure, that poor sister of Dietrich’s will likely die soon if she has not already."
He consumed the last piece he had taken and stood upright on the crab’s body, looking ahead.
"If we meet her, I will be magnanimous enough to offer her shelter.
In the end, even across separate Houses, we all seek the same glory."
His eyes carried the bright imperious light of a being who had stripped every external layer away and found that what remained was entirely comfortable with what it was.
"The glory of Gilded Ones."
His Custodes finished her portion and stood beside him, her breathing steadied, her Source expression cycling back toward functional.
Arjun looked at the dark landscape with the expression of a being who had located the horizon and found it his for the taking!

He stepped off the crab’s body and moved into the dark, and his Custodes followed, and behind them the crab’s slowly dimming Source remained on the dark sand like a marker of where something had ended so that something else could continue.

chapters.title: Chapter 5248: Survival! III
paragraphs: The honey badger tasted like something that had been absorbing Infinity for a very long time and had not wasted any of it.

Noah ate voraciously, the hunger of this place pressing against him with a directness that his cultivated existence had never permitted, every bite landing with the satisfaction of something the body was insisting upon rather than requesting. Beside him, Eon, Ubergulden Adelheid, ate more carefully, with the composure of a being who had more composure available to her at baseline, but ate consistently, her golden Source expression stabilizing visibly with each piece consumed.
They kept their eyes on the surrounding dark.

The beach stretched around them in two directions. Behind them, the obsidian waters churned with the patient menace of something that had a Fourth Scale Eel in it and was not concerned about this fact. Ahead, the terrain divided into two distinct possibilities. To the left, jagged rocks rose from the dark sand in irregular formations that grew taller and denser further inland, the shapes suggesting caves and overhangs and the kind of geography that had defensible positions inside it. To the right, the rocks gave way to coarser sand and sparse ground cover, and in that direction, at the edge of his one-mile perception limit, the faint suggestion of something taller than rock, trees, or what passed for trees here.
Two paths.

Noah ate and thought about which one, and also thought about whether the extreme amplification of every biological function this place imposed was going to extend to the functions he was currently less interested in contemplating, and decided that was a problem for future Noah.
Eon broke the silence.

"Many Gilded Ones will not survive this."She was not looking at him when she said it. She was looking at the dark landscape with the composed certainty of someone delivering an assessment they had already fully made. "They won’t because they can’t. They are inherently prideful, arrogant, and convinced that Existence was designed as their personal velvet cushion. To be stripped down to their Source alone, to have every layer of their engineered armor peeled away until they are naked and raw, is a trauma they aren’t equipped to handle. Adapting is hard when your entire identity is built on the fact that you’ve never had to."
She paused to eat.

"They will try to walk on these lands like they still wear the crown. They will bark commands at the wind and expect the dirt to bow. And they will fail. They will become meals for monstrous Source beasts, torn apart and digested and returned to the mud before they even realize Existence has stopped listening to them." Her expression did not change. "That is the reality. That is the situation. It is messy, it is gruesome, and it is happening right now."
Noah did not disagree.
She turned to look at him, and her eyes moved across his figure with the same unhurried assessment they had conducted earlier, then settled on his face with a different quality.

"But let’s talk about something else that doesn’t add up." Her voice carried the precision of a being who had been constructing a question for several minutes and had finished constructing it."I am Silurian Paleozoic. As far as I knew only moments ago, whatever changes you had undergone placed you at Ordovician Paleozoic at most. And yet you are doing things that shouldn’t be possible in any version of reality I’ve ever encountered."
She leaned forward slightly.

"How can you do what you do? How can you bridge a gap that eons of Gilded engineering haven’t been able to touch? I don’t care about the smoke and the mirrors or the grandiose declarations you make to others. I want the truth. Is it truly just linked to Infinity? What is in your existence that allows you to do what you do?"
Her eyes were shining and still moving across him in the way this place made eyes move.
"Just what are you, really?"
BOOM!
Noah finished the last piece of the honey badger, crimson-gold running down his chin, and smiled.
"Ubergulden Adelheid—"
"Eon."
She said it quietly but directly. Her eyes held his with the expression of a being making a deliberate choice.
"There are no others here. Just call me Eon."
HUUM!

Her Bounded identity. The name she had carried across the eons she had spent living as Bounded rather than Gilded. He felt the weight of it being offered in this stripped place where everything was its irreducible self, and found the weight appropriate.
His smile widened.
"Eon." He said the name once to confirm he had received it. "I am just built a bit differently compared to most. I’ll tell you what I can in time."
He stood and looked at the area around the honey badger’s consumed Source.
"But right now we have to move."

The reasoning was simple and he did not elaborate beyond what was necessary. A Source beast had been killed here. The energy of the kill was radiating outward into the surrounding environment in a way that other creatures in the area could feel, and creatures that could feel it would move toward it. Some to scavenge. Some to investigate. Some because they had learned that fresh kills attracted other existences and fresh existences were better meals than cold Source residue. The beach around them was already a less safe location than it had been twenty minutes ago, and it had not been a safe location then.
He looked at the two directions.

"We need shelter before whatever passes for night here deepens further. We can’t see beyond a mile and neither can most of what’s out here, but some of it can see further than us and all of it knows this terrain better than we do." He looked toward the jagged rock formations rising to the left. "The rocky area gives us high ground. From the peaks we can see movement before it reaches us. If we find a cave or a crevice, we have one entry point to defend instead of every direction at once."
He looked toward the trees on the right.

"The forest has more resources. It also has a canopy, which means things can come from above, and dense coverage means we can be flanked from every angle before we register the approach." He did not labor the conclusion. "We go to the rocks."
Eon looked at both directions and nodded once, the assessment accepted without requiring further argument.

Noah took the first step toward the jagged formations and she fell in beside him, and behind them the cooling residue of the honey badger’s Source continued its slow fade into the dark sand of the beach.

Somewhere in the dark to their right, at the outer edge of his mile of perception, something moved with the unhurried directness of a being that had registered the kill and was coming to see what else the area offered.
They moved faster.

chapters.title: Chapter 5249: Survival! IV
paragraphs: The rocky terrain was genuinely fun!

Noah did not examine this feeling too closely, but it was there, running beneath his careful attention to the dark and the sounds of the Source Lands around them. He had not felt this kind of adversity for a long time. Not the managed adversity of THE Wandering Territories where he had arrived with THE Infinite Tongue and a Primus Apeiron form and proceeded to scatter several thousand Gilded Ones across Observable Existence.

Raw adversity! A mile of perception. No body. Hunger falling by the minute. Unknown creatures in the dark. Unknown creatures in the dark that could kill him if he was not paying attention, which was the kind of adversity that produced the kind of presence he had not felt in his mind since the early apocalypse years.
He was enjoying himself!

He moved through the jagged rock formations with the calm confidence of a being who had elected to be here, his Galdr Source multicolored and steady in the ambient dark, his eyes bright as they tracked the terrain ahead and the terrain to either side and the terrain above without urgency but without gaps.
Behind him, Eon moved carefully.
"These stones..." She had stopped, crouching to examine something near the base of a jutting rock formation.
She pulled her hand back. A thin line of gold on her fingertip, genuine and immediate, the Source Lands making no accommodations for the gold skin of an Ubergulden Royal.
Noah stopped.

He looked at the crystalline obsidian formations embedded in the jagged rock around them, running his Galdr Source light across the surfaces to map their positions. The crystalline clusters appeared at irregular intervals, their edges catching the ambient dark in ways that made them slightly more visible than the surrounding rock, but not enough for someone moving carefully to guarantee they avoided every one.
He crouched.

His hands closed around three of the largest crystalline outcroppings with his Galdr Source blazing gold-multicolored around his palms, the compressed energy of his Source bearing down on the material with the directness of a being applying what he had available to the problem in front of him.

The crystalline stone broke along the lines he pressed, shearing cleanly rather than shattering, and he pulled three jagged lengths free, each one roughly the length of his forearm, each one with a natural point at one end from where it had broken.
He bathed his hands in Infinity.

THE Infinite Tongue directed the obsidian material at the blunt ends of each piece, the grinding and reshaping slow but functional, the Tongue convincing the crystalline substance to smooth itself into a grip rather than forcing it. The grip end rounded. The pointed end stayed sharp. Three times, then a fourth for himself.
He handed three to Eon.
She looked at the weapons and then at his hands with an expression that was recalibrating something.
He started moving again.

The cavern opening presented itself in the face of a larger rock formation, a darkness within the general darkness that his perception mapped as a space extending approximately thirty feet inward with a single entry and no additional exits. One way in. No way to be flanked from behind.
He held up a hand.
Eon stopped.
He went in alone.
He had covered approximately six feet of the cavern’s interior when something shot from the ceiling without warning, the movement fast and low and aimed at his face. Noah raised his hand.

THE Infinite Vector caught the creature’s momentum mid-air and held it, the forward force redirected sideways by a fraction sufficient to stop its trajectory dead, the creature suspended in the space in front of him at approximately chest height, its limbs cycling uselessly in the frozen direction.
He looked at it.

It was compact and dense, roughly the size of a large dog, its exterior composed of layered rock-like plates that interlocked across its body like the shell of something that had been designed to live in exactly this kind of terrain. Four legs, wide-set, built for ceiling movement as much as floor movement. Its eyes were small and deeply set in the rock-plate face, currently blazing with the crimson of a creature that was very angry about no longer moving.

|Source Creature: Seidr Cave Mantler. First Demarcation. Long-term resident of THE Source Lands’ rocky regions. Territorial. Ambush predator operating from ceilings and overhangs. Source technique- Plate Lock: can harden its rock plates to absorb significant force from direct strikes. Most effective against brute force approaches. Bypassed by piercing or internal damage.|
Noah smiled.

He drove his crystalline spear into the gap between the Cave Mantler’s neck plates and pushed Infinity into the wound directly, the multicolored current moving through the entry point and distributing through the creature’s interior with the thoroughness of liquid filling a container. The blazing crimson of its eyes dimmed in segments.
He caught the body as the Vector released it.

He directed the obsidian Infinity from the surrounding cave walls to form a bubble around the body, the dark material compressing around the creature and sealing it, containing the smell and the dimming Source light inside the seal. Preserved. He set it against the cave wall.
"Clear," he called out.
Eon entered.

He moved through the full interior of the cavern with his Source expression lighting the space, mapping the ceiling for additional residents, checking the floor for anything embedded in the rock. Nothing. He took inventory of the entry angle, the ceiling height, the width of the passage at the narrowest point where it could be defended from.
He went to the back and sat down.

Eon came to the back and sat beside him, close enough that her shoulder was near his, her golden Source expression still cycling at slightly elevated intensity from the last hour of continuous alertness. She breathed out.
The breath carried something it had not carried outside.

Noah looked at her face in the multicolored light of his Source and at the gold of her expression cycling warmly in the dark cave and felt the amplified pulse of this place pressing against his lust with the patient insistence it had been pressing with since they arrived. He did not act on it. He put it under things controlled.
He thought, instead, about how universal this moment was.

Power or no power, cultivation or no cultivation, Gilded engineering or Bounded scrapping ...everyone wanted to feel safe. Everyone wanted to stop moving and breathe out. Those with power built the safety themselves. Those without it had to find something powerful enough to stand near and trust that the proximity would hold. He had been that proximity for people across the full span of his climb. It was a role he had never applied for and had never stopped occupying.
He leaned back against the cave wall and closed his eyes.
The amplified lust of this place pressed. He did not move.
"Keep my mind busy," he said. "Tell me about your time before you became THE Secretive Eon."
A pause.
Eon blinked at the request. He did not look at her to observe it, but he felt the small shift in her Source expression that corresponded to being asked something she had not expected.
Then she moved and turned. She put her back against the smooth section of rock beside him and pulled her knees up and looked at the cave ceiling.
She began to speak.
The words came slowly at first. Then less slowly. Then with the continuous ease of something that had been waiting for someone to ask and had simply been waiting for a long time.
Hours began to pass as Noah listned to THE Secretive Eon while waiting for light to come so he could really begin his growth and conquest of THE Source Lands!

chapters.title: Chapter 5250: Persevere! I
paragraphs: The hours in the cave had not been idle.

While Eon talked, Noah listened and gathered, and what he gathered was the sensation of his Source as a thing he could actually examine now that the immediate pressures of arrival had settled into the background rhythm of a place he was beginning to understand rather than simply react to.
He pressed his awareness inward and compared.
|Source Type Analysis:|

|Seidr Source- First Demarcation: Presents as vapor. The Source energy of a Seidr existence is diffuse, spreading outward from the core in loose filaments that extend further than their density warrants. The vapor quality means Seidr Sources register as larger than they functionally are, their energy spread thin across their expression. Under pressure from the ambient elements of THE Source Lands, Seidr Source filaments are easily disrupted and slow to reconverge, which produces the rapid Satiety depletion most First Demarcation entities experience. The diffusion works in one narrow context: a Seidr Source can sense a wider area than its strength suggests, the loose filaments reaching further than denser expressions travel. This makes them better at detection than confrontation.|

|Galdr Source- Second Demarcation: Presents as liquid. Dense, viscous, coherent. Where Seidr disperses, Galdr pools. The energy stays concentrated at the core and moves as a unified substance rather than as filaments, which means ambient pressure hits it with less effect, as there are fewer loose edges to pull apart. Galdr Sources deplete slower under standard conditions and recover faster from partial depletion because the concentration provides a stable reservoir to draw from rather than a dispersed field to reconsolidate. The density also produces a secondary effect: other Sources in proximity register the Galdr’s presence more accurately than they register a Seidr’s, the concentrated mass broadcasting more clearly into the environment. In THE Source Lands, this translates to other entities knowing where a Galdr Source is. The advantage in strength is accompanied by reduced capacity for concealment.|

|Source Strengthening Factors: Infinity is the primary contributor for beings who carry it, its density directly translating to Source viscosity and coherence. Observable Force provides structural stability, reducing the rate of ambient sapping. Cause links add depth to the Source’s foundational coherence- a Source tied to a Prime Cause does not merely exist, it exists in alignment with one of the foundational truths of Observable Existence, and the alignment provides resistance that neither Infinity nor Observable Force alone can replicate. Origin lineage contributes a factor that cannot be cultivated: the proximity of one’s originating existence to THE First Cause’s emergence weighs on Source strength in ways that are fixed rather than developed. What one is, at the deepest level, contributes to Source coherence independent of what one has built.|
Noah absorbed this and felt the satisfaction of a system he understood becoming visible around him.

He liked the simplicity of it. No Civilizations. No engineering. No architectural layers of accumulated cultivation. Just what he was at the irreducible level and THE Infinite Tongue, which lived there rather than in any of the layers that had been stripped away. His power here was not diminished in the ways it would have diminished a Gilded One. It was different.
Different was workable!
On the ninth hour since their arrival, the darkness shifted.

It did not lighten gradually the way dawn lightened a sky. It receded in a wave, the darkness pulling back from above first, the withdrawal uncovering something that replaced it with a thoroughness that made gradual feel like an insufficient concept.
Noah rose.
Eon came up alongside him and they moved out of the cave mouth together to see what light meant in a place that had no sun.
He stood on the rocks and looked up and felt his eyes open wide.
Above THE Source Lands, where sky should have been and where absolute dark had been for nine hours, flowers were blooming.
Flowers bloomed in thr skies!

Not small. The scale of them was wrong in the specific way that things in this place operated at scales Observable Existence did not use as default. Each flower was a luminous golden formation the size of a small sun, their petals unfurling from central points in the upper dark with the slow deliberate motion of something that had been waiting for its hour and had found it!

Dozens of them. Each one blazing with golden light that carried warmth along with it, genuine warmth that reached the rocky terrain below and pressed against Noah’s Source with the sensation of something nourishing rather than merely illuminating. They bloomed in clusters and individually, distributed across the upper dark in no geometric pattern, simply present wherever they had chosen to be present.

|Source Suns- THE Illumination Flowers of THE Source Lands: Natural phenomenon unique to this environment. Bloom on a cycle that does not correspond to any external temporal measurement. Duration of bloom varies. The golden light they produce carries a trace of THE Primordial Source’s ambient energy, which is why the darkness of THE Source Lands is absolute during non-bloom periods- the Illumination Flowers are the only light source this place produces, and THE Primordial Source’s ambient energy does not provide illumination in the way Infinity does. Their light accelerates Source sapping slightly but also accelerates Source recovery from consumption, producing a net positive environment for active hunting. During bloom, all Sources become more active and more visible.|
Noah looked down from the flowers to the terrain around them and found it revealed for the first time.

The rocky formations they had moved through extended upward into a mountainscape that his one-mile perception had not been able to fully map in the dark, the peaks rising into the lower reaches of the bloom-lit sky with the permanence of geography that had existed long before any arrival had occurred.

Behind them, the beach and the dark clear waters of the obsidian sea extended outward without visible end, calmer now that the Source Eel had retreated to whatever depth it preferred, the surface carrying the gold of the Illumination Flowers reflected across its darkness.
And to the right.

The forest line rose at the outer edge of his perception, and what rose there was not the sparse suggestion of trees he had registered in the dark before. The Illumination Flowers’ gold reached across the misty obsidian-gold shroud covering that region and revealed the shapes within it, and the shapes were massive and distinct and wrong in the best possible way.

Ancient baobabs with trunks wider than the cave they had sheltered in, their roots spilling outward across the ground in networks that suggested their root systems extended further underground than their canopies extended above.

Banyan-like structures with aerial roots descending from their canopies to form secondary trunks, each secondary trunk itself large enough to constitute a forest feature independently. Towering fig trees whose branches spread in the specific sacred geometry of things that had grown according to older logic than ordinary biology followed, their bark shimmering with the obsidian-gold of ambient Source energy absorbed across uncountable eons of growth here.
And moving through the canopy between these, something that was not quite vine and not quite root but moved with the slow purpose of a living thing that had decided where it was going.
All of it shrouded in the misty obsidian-gold light. All of it vast!

His Source pulled toward it. The sensation was physical in the way that hunger was physical, a directional urgency from the deepest available layer of what he was, pointing at the forest the way a compass pointed at a fixed referent. Resources. Wonders!
His Source broadcasting that the forest held things it wanted to consume and that the wanting was serious.
He was still looking at it when the beach moved.
From the obsidian sand below the rocky terrain, shapes emerged!

sentences.text: The hours in the cave had not been idle.

While Eon talked, Noah listened and gathered, and what he gathered was the sensation of his Source as a thing he could actually examine now that the immediate pressures of arrival had settled into the background rhythm of a place he was beginning to understand rather than simply react to.
He pressed his awareness inward and compared.
|Source Type Analysis:|
|Seidr Source- First Demarcation: Presents as vapor.
The Source energy of a Seidr existence is diffuse, spreading outward from the core in loose filaments that extend further than their density warrants.
The vapor quality means Seidr Sources register as larger than they functionally are, their energy spread thin across their expression.

Under pressure from the ambient elements of THE Source Lands, Seidr Source filaments are easily disrupted and slow to reconverge, which produces the rapid Satiety depletion most First Demarcation entities experience.
The diffusion works in one narrow context: a Seidr Source can sense a wider area than its strength suggests, the loose filaments reaching further than denser expressions travel.
This makes them better at detection than confrontation.|
|Galdr Source- Second Demarcation: Presents as liquid.
Dense, viscous, coherent.
Where Seidr disperses, Galdr pools.

The energy stays concentrated at the core and moves as a unified substance rather than as filaments, which means ambient pressure hits it with less effect, as there are fewer loose edges to pull apart.

Galdr Sources deplete slower under standard conditions and recover faster from partial depletion because the concentration provides a stable reservoir to draw from rather than a dispersed field to reconsolidate.

The density also produces a secondary effect: other Sources in proximity register the Galdr’s presence more accurately than they register a Seidr’s, the concentrated mass broadcasting more clearly into the environment.
In THE Source Lands, this translates to other entities knowing where a Galdr Source is.
The advantage in strength is accompanied by reduced capacity for concealment.|
|Source Strengthening Factors: Infinity is the primary contributor for beings who carry it, its density directly translating to Source viscosity and coherence.
Observable Force provides structural stability, reducing the rate of ambient sapping.

Cause links add depth to the Source’s foundational coherence- a Source tied to a Prime Cause does not merely exist, it exists in alignment with one of the foundational truths of Observable Existence, and the alignment provides resistance that neither Infinity nor Observable Force alone can replicate.

Origin lineage contributes a factor that cannot be cultivated: the proximity of one’s originating existence to THE First Cause’s emergence weighs on Source strength in ways that are fixed rather than developed.
What one is, at the deepest level, contributes to Source coherence independent of what one has built.|
Noah absorbed this and felt the satisfaction of a system he understood becoming visible around him.
He liked the simplicity of it.
No Civilizations.
No engineering.
No architectural layers of accumulated cultivation.
Just what he was at the irreducible level and THE Infinite Tongue, which lived there rather than in any of the layers that had been stripped away.
His power here was not diminished in the ways it would have diminished a Gilded One.
It was different.
Different was workable!
On the ninth hour since their arrival, the darkness shifted.
It did not lighten gradually the way dawn lightened a sky.
It receded in a wave, the darkness pulling back from above first, the withdrawal uncovering something that replaced it with a thoroughness that made gradual feel like an insufficient concept.
Noah rose.
Eon came up alongside him and they moved out of the cave mouth together to see what light meant in a place that had no sun.
He stood on the rocks and looked up and felt his eyes open wide.
Above THE Source Lands, where sky should have been and where absolute dark had been for nine hours, flowers were blooming.
Flowers bloomed in thr skies!
Not small.
The scale of them was wrong in the specific way that things in this place operated at scales Observable Existence did not use as default.

Each flower was a luminous golden formation the size of a small sun, their petals unfurling from central points in the upper dark with the slow deliberate motion of something that had been waiting for its hour and had found it!
Dozens of them.

Each one blazing with golden light that carried warmth along with it, genuine warmth that reached the rocky terrain below and pressed against Noah’s Source with the sensation of something nourishing rather than merely illuminating.
They bloomed in clusters and individually, distributed across the upper dark in no geometric pattern, simply present wherever they had chosen to be present.

chapters.title: Chapter 5251: Persevere! II
paragraphs: One at first, then three, then a dozen, then dozens, the obsidian-gold carapaces of large crabs breaking the sand surface and hauling themselves upright in the golden bloom light, each one the size of a large table, their eyes and bodies glittering with Seidr Source light that brightened as the Illumination Flowers above reached their full bloom.
The crabs looked around.
They looked at each other.
Then one of them raised a claw.
What followed could only be described as a dance.

It started with the one who had raised the claw, the movement rhythmic and deliberate, the claw dropping and rising in a pattern that carried the specific quality of something practiced rather than improvised.

Then the crab beside it picked up the pattern and added its own claw motion, the two of them locked into the same rhythm. Then three more joined. Then ten. Then all of them, dozens of obsidian-gold crabs on the dark beach moving in synchronized sequence, claws rising and falling in staggered waves, bodies shifting sideways in the specific two-step that crabs executed when moving, the whole assembly producing a coordinated spectacle that was genuinely terrible to classify using any existing vocabulary!
HUUM!
Around them, as the dance progressed, their Seidr Sources began to resonate.

Tendrils of obsidian Infinity and Observable Force extended between the dancing crabs and connected their Source expressions, the shared rhythm producing a shared amplification, each crab’s Seidr vapor thickening slightly from the energy circulating through the synchronized group. The dance was not decorative. It was cultivation!
Whatever this ritual produced for them, they performed it every time the Illumination Flowers bloomed, and they had been performing it long enough that they were very good at it!
Noah watched them.
Eon watched them beside him with incredulity.
Noah looked closer as Infinity provided him waves of information!
|Source Creature Identification: Seidr Crater Crabs.|

|First Demarcation. Long-term residents of THE Source Lands’ coastal regions. Highly social, which in most environments would be considered a charming quality. In THE Source Lands, it primarily means there are more of them than one would like.|
|Behavioral Note: Seidr Crater Crabs are among the few species in THE Source Lands that have developed cooperative survival strategies rather than simply eating each other until one remains.|

|Ritual Analysis: The synchronized movement you are observing is designatedTHE Bloom Rite. Performed exclusively during Illumination Flower cycles, the Rite functions as a collective Source resonance amplification, the Seidr vapor of each participating individual interlinking with adjacent participants to form a temporary shared Source network. The rhythm is not arbitrary. Precise timing between participants is required for the resonance to accumulate rather than cancel. The crabs have had a very long time to practice. They are, objectively, better at this than most things one will encounter here are at anything.|

|Effect: Each completed Bloom Rite cycle increases participant Satiety by approximately 4% and marginally densifies individual Seidr vapor expression for a duration following the Rite. The communal nature means a lone Seidr Crater Crab gains nothing. This has not stopped lone Seidr Crater Crabs from attempting the dance. It is among the saddest things in THE Source Lands.|

|Threat Assessment: Moderate. The Seidr Crater Crab’s primary offensive capability is its claws, which are stronger than they appear, and its secondary offensive capability is that there are dozens of them and they are watching you right now.|
|They noticed you some time ago when you noticed them. They chose the dance anyway.|
It was a ridiculous thing to see, but it was grand!
The crabs were very good at their dance!

Noah watched them with appreciation of someone who had not expected the first thing the Illumination Flowers revealed to be synchronized Source ritual choreography, and was finding the unexpected nature of it one of the more charming details of THE Source Lands so far.
But...
Natural selection, he thought. Kill or be killed!

In existence, the equation never changed regardless of the domain or the scale or the beings involved. Even here. Even these crabs, with their bloom ritual and their shared resonance and their genuine proficiency at a thing that had clearly been refined across many Illumination cycles.
Even them....he may have to hunt them!
But...
He did not finish the thought.
BOOM!

Obsidian lightning smashed down from the upper dark in seven simultaneous strikes, each one finding a Seidr Crater Crab with the precision of attacks that had been aimed rather than scattered, the carapaces of the struck crabs shattering inward under the impact as the lightning chained between the strikes to hit adjacent crabs in the same sequence.
A massive raptor came in behind the lightning.

It moved low and fast from the tree line, its body surrounded by obsidian Infinity shaped into continuous arcing lightning that rolled across its scales with the easy comfort of an ability that had been practiced into instinct. It was large, its frame carrying the dense musculature of something that had been hunting in THE Source Lands for long enough, its eyes carrying the cruel intelligence of a Galdr Source predator who had developed opinions about its prey.
It drove its jaws into the nearest crab with broken carapace and ate without slowing, still moving, the eating and the hunting simultaneous.
A circular ring of lightning expanded outward from its body and settled into the sand at a radius that enclosed the remaining crabs in a crackling boundary that surged when any crab touched it.
The raptor looked at the contained crabs.
"Wait for me, my little snacks."

Behind it, at the edge of the tree line where the massive flora had revealed itself in the bloom light, other Utahraptors watched from the elevated branches. All Seidr. First Demarcation. Observing with the relaxed attention of beings confident that what was happening was going to conclude in a predictable way.
Inside the lightning ring, the crabs did not wait!

They surged toward the Utahraptor with their claws raised and their Seidr Sources blazing with the resonance the Bloom Rite had just amplified, the collective brightness of them pressing against the encirclement with the desperate energy of things that had survived long enough to know that not fighting was not an option.
Noah shook his head as a bright smile bloomed on his face.
He looked at Eon.
"Let’s go."
He jumped!

chapters.title: Chapter 5252: Persevere! III
paragraphs: His Galdr Source took the jump far past what any ordinary jump should have covered, the multicolored density of his Infinity compressing against the ground and releasing upward in a single motion that carried him across the distance between the rocks and the lightning ring with the arc of something moving with intention rather than physics!

He came down inside the ring beside the crabs, and his Source blazed outward when he landed, multicolored and brilliant, the impact sending a ring of displaced sand outward in every direction from the landing point, Eon arrived beside him soon after with an imperial gaze.
The Utahraptor looked at him.
Its cruel eyes moved across Noah’s figure, and something behind those eyes decided on a conclusion quickly!

"Another pair of golden humans appear." It ate a crab while it spoke, the multitasking effortless. "Haha, look at you. Standing there in your stupid form with all that confidence. You are nothing more than golden humans. Fragile. Polished. Pathetic." It ate another crab.

"Many of your kind have crawled out of the woodwork recently. I’ve had to clear the brush. I’ve killed a fair amount, and I must say, you taste better than the common rabble. Your Sources are unique. Intricate. A pleasant change of menu after so much bland, repetitive existence."
It began moving toward Noah, the lightning rolling across its body in lazy arcs.

"And here you are. You’ve saved me the exercise. You’ve descended and landed right in my lap. For that small mercy, I’ll be kind. I’ll make your transition quick." The cruel eyes carried no mercy behind the promise.

"You always have that look. That wide-eyed stuttering shock as the light goes out. As if the laws of Existence were written to exclude you from the grave. As if your power granted you a seat at a table that doesn’t exist."
It stopped and drew itself to full height.
"You think you are the sun? You are nothing. Death is not a suggestion. It is not a request. It is a command. Death comes to all. Death. Comes. To. All!"
BOOM!
"Come receive yours!"

The tendrils of lightning crashed outward from the Utahraptor toward Noah and Eon, the strikes fast and converging, the obsidian Infinity within them carrying the weight of a Galdr Source that had been generating lightning attacks for longer than Noah had been alive!
Noah scowled.
His smile was brutal.
"I was looking for a Galdr Source to test." He met the Utahraptor’s eyes. "You’ll do just fine."
He moved into the lightning.

THE Infinite Vector caught the first tendril mid-arc and redirected it sideways, the lightning curving away from its original trajectory and dissipating into the sand. The second tendril hit the Vector’s passive field and found its direction rewritten before it reached Noah’s position. The Utahraptor’s eyes narrowed as the attacks failed to arrive and Noah covered the distance between them in the interval the Utahraptor spent processing why the lightning had not landed.
His fist found the Utahraptor’s jaw.

The Galdr Source behind the strike hit the Utahraptor’s foundation directly, not a cultivated attack but a Source against Source contact, the multicolored density of Noah’s Galdr pressing into the Utahraptor’s obsidian Galdr at the point of impact!
The Utahraptor’s head snapped sideways and it disengaged with a speed that was genuine, the cruel eyes recalibrating as it circled.
It drove two lightning tendrils of infinity from different angles simultaneously, the spread designed to force a choice between blocking one or the other.

Noah rewrote both of their directions with THE Infinite Vector, then pulled the Infinity in the lightning itself toward him rather than letting it dissipate into the sand, the Vector redirecting the energy’s intent from destructive to available, and drove toward the Utahraptor with the borrowed lightning running through his Galdr Source as an additional layer.
BOOM!

The strike landed in the Utahraptor’s midsection and the borrowed lightning discharged through the contact point, the Utahraptor’s own attack returning through its own body from an angle it had not built any defenses against. It went down on one knee!
Noah was already on it, his Source blazing at the top of its current expression as he drove into the Utahraptor’s position with the focused density of a Galdr!

The Utahraptor’s lightning flared desperately and struck at him from multiple directions, the attacks clumsy from the damage accumulating in its foundations, and Noah took the strikes that he took and he kept pressing because the gap between their Source expressions was real and the gap was in his favor and the gap was widening!
He had the Utahraptor’s neck in his grip, the obsidian lightning sputtering through the contact as the Utahraptor’s Galdr Source burned through its available reserves to sustain the resistance!
He pulled back his free hand to end it and obtain a meal of Galdr proportions.
But...
"PERSEVERE!"
BOOM!
The Utahraptor roared it from somewhere beneath the grip.

Obsidian flames erupted from its entire body in a single expanding detonation that drove Noah backward hard enough to cross twenty feet of beach before he arrested the motion, his feet dragging through dark sand as his Galdr Source absorbed the force of the expulsion. He looked at the Utahraptor with wide eyes!
The wounds were gone.

Not healing. Gone. Its Galdr Source burned brighter than it had at the start of the engagement, the obsidian lightning rolling across it with renewed intensity, the cruel eyes blazing with something that had not been present before!
It had used THE Primordial Tongue!
Noah’s eyes shone.
The same word the two Relictus had used in the Bellum Dreamstone’s vision, healing themselves across eighty-one cycles of destruction and emerging stronger from each recovery!
THE Primordial Tongue, accessible here, in THE Source Lands, apparently to a Galdr Source Utahraptor who had been present long enough to find it.

The Seidr Crabs were burrowing frantically into the sand at the edges of the lightning ring, the trembling of things that had just watched something they would normally run from get hit by something worse and get back up!
The Utahraptor stood like a beast emperor in the bloom light, obsidian lightning cascading off it, the other Seidr Utahraptors at the tree line watching now with different postures than before.
Noah looked at Eon.

"Why don’t you go handle those Seidr ones at the tree line." He nodded toward the watching group. "You haven’t been pulling on my Infinity yet so start doing it now. Pull on my power and you should be more than okay."
He turned back to the Utahraptor, his brutal smile not having moved.
"I...want to have a very good time with this one to see just how long it can Persevere."
Information flowed!
|Source Creature Identification: Galdr Stormcaller Utahraptor.|

|Second Demarcation. An Apex predator of THE Source Lands’ coastal and forest border region in this immediate vicinity. Has been here long enough to develop a personality, which in most contexts would suggest wisdom and depth. In this context it suggests it has eaten a very large number of things and has had considerable time to feel good about this.|
|Behavioral Note: The Galdr Stormcaller Utahraptor is among the few Second Demarcation creatures nearby to have independently developed a sustained lightning-based Infinity expression.|

|Lightning Encirclement Ability: THE Stormwall. A contained ring of obsidian lightning generated from the creature’s Galdr Source, deployed to prevent prey from escaping while the Stormcaller addresses other prey. Functions as intended.|

|Predatory Note: The Galdr Stormcaller Utahraptor prefers to monologue before engaging. This has never once caused it to lose a fight. It has, however, occasionally allowed prey to escape during the monologue.|
|Threat Assessment: Moderate. It is larger than you. It is faster than you probably expect. It controls lightning. It has given a speech at you, which means it is confident.|

It drove two lightning tendrils of infinity from different angles simultaneously, the spread designed to force a choice between blocking one or the other.

Noah rewrote both of their directions with THE Infinite Vector, then pulled the Infinity in the lightning itself toward him rather than letting it dissipate into the sand, the Vector redirecting the energy’s intent from destructive to available, and drove toward the Utahraptor with the borrowed lightning running through his Galdr Source as an additional layer.
BOOM!

The strike landed in the Utahraptor’s midsection and the borrowed lightning discharged through the contact point, the Utahraptor’s own attack returning through its own body from an angle it had not built any defenses against.
It went down on one knee!
Noah was already on it, his Source blazing at the top of its current expression as he drove into the Utahraptor’s position with the focused density of a Galdr!

The Utahraptor’s lightning flared desperately and struck at him from multiple directions, the attacks clumsy from the damage accumulating in its foundations, and Noah took the strikes that he took and he kept pressing because the gap between their Source expressions was real and the gap was in his favor and the gap was widening!
He had the Utahraptor’s neck in his grip, the obsidian lightning sputtering through the contact as the Utahraptor’s Galdr Source burned through its available reserves to sustain the resistance!
He pulled back his free hand to end it and obtain a meal of Galdr proportions.
But...
"PERSEVERE!"
BOOM!
The Utahraptor roared it from somewhere beneath the grip.

Obsidian flames erupted from its entire body in a single expanding detonation that drove Noah backward hard enough to cross twenty feet of beach before he arrested the motion, his feet dragging through dark sand as his Galdr Source absorbed the force of the expulsion.
He looked at the Utahraptor with wide eyes!
The wounds were gone.
Not healing.
Gone.

Its Galdr Source burned brighter than it had at the start of the engagement, the obsidian lightning rolling across it with renewed intensity, the cruel eyes blazing with something that had not been present before!
It had used THE Primordial Tongue!
Noah’s eyes shone.
The same word the two Relictus had used in the Bellum Dreamstone’s vision, healing themselves across eighty-one cycles of destruction and emerging stronger from each recovery!
THE Primordial Tongue, accessible here, in THE Source Lands, apparently to a Galdr Source Utahraptor who had been present long enough to find it.

The Seidr Crabs were burrowing frantically into the sand at the edges of the lightning ring, the trembling of things that had just watched something they would normally run from get hit by something worse and get back up!
The Utahraptor stood like a beast emperor in the bloom light, obsidian lightning cascading off it, the other Seidr Utahraptors at the tree line watching now with different postures than before.
Noah looked at Eon.
"Why don’t you go handle those Seidr ones at the tree line." He nodded toward the watching group.
"You haven’t been pulling on my Infinity yet so start doing it now.
Pull on my power and you should be more than okay."
He turned back to the Utahraptor, his brutal smile not having moved.
"I...want to have a very good time with this one to see just how long it can Persevere."
Information flowed!
|Source Creature Identification: Galdr Stormcaller Utahraptor.|
|Second Demarcation.
An Apex predator of THE Source Lands’ coastal and forest border region in this immediate vicinity.
Has been here long enough to develop a personality, which in most contexts would suggest wisdom and depth.
In this context it suggests it has eaten a very large number of things and has had considerable time to feel good about this.|
|Behavioral Note: The Galdr Stormcaller Utahraptor is among the few Second Demarcation creatures nearby to have independently developed a sustained lightning-based Infinity expression.|
|Lightning Encirclement Ability: THE Stormwall.
A contained ring of obsidian lightning generated from the creature’s Galdr Source, deployed to prevent prey from escaping while the Stormcaller addresses other prey.
Functions as intended.|
|Predatory Note: The Galdr Stormcaller Utahraptor prefers to monologue before engaging.
This has never once caused it to lose a fight.
It has, however, occasionally allowed prey to escape during the monologue.|
|Threat Assessment: Moderate.
It is larger than you.
It is faster than you probably expect.
It controls lightning.
It has given a speech at you, which means it is confident.|

chapters.title: Chapter 5253: Persevere! IV
paragraphs: Noah coated his hands.

The obsidian Infinity from the surrounding beach answered THE Infinite Tongue without argument, pulling toward his grip and compressing into a dense layer across his knuckles and forearms, the Galdr Source concentrating it further until the coating carried the viscous density of his full Source expression rather than the loose ambient material it had been before he touched it. His fists burned obsidian-multicolored, the darkness of the Infinity threading through with the gold of his Galdr.
He moved toward the Utahraptor!
His footwork was fluid and low, his body swaying lightly with brutality as each step rolled into the next with the continuous momentum of water finding its way downhill!

The Utahraptor drove its lightning toward him and he rolled under it, the motion carrying him beneath the strike and into the Utahraptor’s throat, and he came up with a punch coated with his source to hit the Utahraptor’s jaw from below!
BOOM!
The obsidian coating on his arm discharged on contact.
The Utahraptor’s head snapped back.

It came back with a low sweep of its tail and a lightning tendril from its right, the combination designed for the specific geometry of something that had fought many things and built patterns around what worked. Noah stepped over the tail with a sweeping lateral kick that changed his position without stopping his momentum, the kick connecting with the Utahraptor’s knee on the way past, and the lightning tendril hit the space he had just vacated.
He was already behind it.

His heel came down across the back of the Utahraptor’s neck with the full compression of his Galdr Source behind it and the obsidian Infinity coating making the contact point a concentrated delivery of everything he was currently carrying.
BOOM!
The Utahraptor went down hard.
"PERSEVERE!"

Obsidian flames. The Source healing again, the wounds closing in the surge of Primordial Tongue authority, the Utahraptor rising back to its feet with the specific quality of something that had found its bottom and bounced off it. Its lightning was brighter this time. Its eyes burned harder.
Noah watched the recovery with genuine interest.
He moved back in as he loved getting physical!

The rhythm of the engagement settled into something he was reading and the Utahraptor was not, his footwork carrying him around the Utahraptor’s committed strikes rather than through them, the swaying lateral motion making him a target that resolved in different positions than the targeting had accounted for. He hit it from three different angles in a sequence that did not give the Utahraptor time to establish a defensive posture between impacts, his hands and feet working in the rolling continuous combination of someone who had decided the fight was an exercise in expression rather than survival.
The Utahraptor’s lightning fought back with everything it had.

Noah’s Vector redirected what it could and his Source absorbed what it couldn’t redirect, the obsidian strikes landing on him with decreasing effect as the fight deepened and the Utahraptor’s reserves burned through their recovered fullness faster with each Persevere cycle.
The second Persevere came slower than the first.

The wounds it healed were the same wounds, or similar enough, but the roar had less behind it. The Primordial Tongue cost something. Using it repeatedly cost more of something, the same word drawing from the same well and finding the well slightly less full each time.
Noah kept going as he wanted to learn everything.

He kept the rhythm. Low, flowing, continuous. Hit and move and hit from somewhere else and move again, his footwork never quite stopping, the fight a sustained expression of everything he had been doing rather than a series of separate exchanges. The Utahraptor’s responses slowed by increments small enough that each individual increment was unremarkable and the accumulation was devastating.
Third Persevere. The flames that erupted were shorter lived. The brightness they produced faded faster!
Fourth Persevere. A long pause before the word arrived, the Utahraptor finding it from somewhere deep, the voice carrying the sound of something that was very tired and had not yet admitted this.
Noah leaped.

He came down with both feet across the Utahraptor’s back in the specific concentrated delivery of someone landing on something they intended to stay landed on, the obsidian coating on his feet discharging completely into the contact point, the full density of his Galdr Source driving straight down through the Utahraptor’s foundations.
The Utahraptor trembled.
It tried.

The shape of Persevere formed somewhere in its chest, the ancient letter of THE Primordial Tongue moving toward expression with the desperate insistence of a word that had saved it four times before and was being asked for a fifth.
It could not make it out.

The Source broke with the exhaustion of something that had held on as long as holding was available and had simply reached the end of how long that was. The Utahraptor’s obsidian lightning went still. Its eyes dimmed from their blazing cruel brightness to something quieter, the light retreating toward the center before it stopped entirely.
From its body, a fragment of obsidian light rose.
Small. The size of his fist! Drifting upward from the collapsed Utahraptor’s Source with the patient certainty of something that knew where it was going.
|A Glorious Battle!|

|Galdr Stormcaller Utahraptor: Defeated. Its Source has been broken through sustained engagement rather than a single overwhelming strike, which required considerably more effort than the single overwhelming strike would have. On the other hand, the sustained engagement was more interesting.|
|Consumption available:The Utahraptor’s body will restore approximately 51% Satiety for a Galdr Source entity. This is a meaningful meal. Eat it.|
|Secondary acquisition:Fragment of the Letter of THE Primordial Tongue- Persevere.|
|The creature accessed THE Primordial Tongue during your engagement. It did not give you this fragment voluntarily. You took it by breaking its Source before it could use the letter a fifth time.|

|The Primordial Tongue operates through complete letters rather than fragments. You currently hold one fragment of Persevere. Obtaining four additional fragments of this letter will allow your Source to fully grasp its weavings and utilize it as the creature did.|
|Note: THE Primordial Tongue is the language of THE Primordial Source.|
|One fragment down. Four to go.|
Noah’s eyes shone brilliantly as he watched the dazzling loot!
This place continued to exceed every known measurement of power and glory as he had to find...4 other fragments to gain acces to another tongue!
