chapters.title: Chapter 5254: THE Strand of Broken Scales I
paragraphs: The crabs held their line with the specific anxiety of creatures that had very recently been inside a lightning ring and had not yet decided whether the current situation was better.
Noah looked at them.
One of them, the largest, began to raise its claw in the opening motion of the Bloom Rite.
"If you begin dancing again," Noah said, "I will fry you and eat the meat. All of you."
The claw lowered.

"Good. Now." He crouched to their eye level, his Galdr Source multicolored and calm around him. "Tell me the locations of any areas you never venture into. Anything in the surrounding region that you avoid. Any Galdr Source beings like the one that killed your people."
The crabs looked at each other.

They began clicking their claws in rapid sequences, the sounds overlapping and rhythmic, and tendrils of obsidian Infinity moved between them as the clicking carried information that the Infinity translated outward. Noah’s Infinite Tongue reached into the ambient communication and pulled what it could, the shape of a region assembling itself from the crab’s collective knowledge into something he could orient around.

They were in a stretch of coast the crabs had no name for but that his Tongue organized asTHE Strand of Broken Scales,a region running several hundred miles along the beach and extending inland to where the forest thickened into terrain the crabs considered categorically non-survivable for their kind. The beach and the rocky terrain behind it were their domain. The forest border was not.
Three areas the crabs never went:

The first was north along the coast, where the dark waters churned in a pattern that suggested something very large moving beneath them at regular intervals. The Source Eel from their arrival was a possibility. Something larger was also a possibility.The crabs had not investigated because the crabs that had investigated had not returned.

The second was inland and east, where the vegetation gave way to a clearing the crabs could sense from the border but approached no closer to. The ambient Source pressure from the clearing registered to them as something that had claimed territory so thoroughly that approaching it produced a specific biological response they had learned to respect.

The third was directly ahead in the deep forest, where the tree canopy had grown so dense that the Illumination Flowers’ light did not reach the ground beneath it, and the things that lived in that permanent dark had developed accordingly.

The Galdr Sources that used Persevere, the crabs communicated through their clicking and their Infinity tendrils, were concentrated in the second area. The clearing. Several of them. They were why nothing else used the clearing.
Noah rose.

He turned and found Eon already walking toward him from the direction of the tree line, her golden skin catching the bloom light with the specific quality of someone who had been through something physical and had not paused to address the evidence of it.

Her figure was dazzling and blood-streaked in equal measure, the obsidian-multicolored Infinity she had borrowed from him still cycling around her as she tore a piece from the Utahraptor leg in her hand with the focused interest of someone whose Satiety was responding well to the input.
She came to stand beside him and chewed and looked at the crabs.

"This place amplifies your emotions considerably." She said it with a thoughtful cadence. "You feel a thrill when you are hunting and eating. It becomes almost bloodthirsty. As if seeking dominance is simply in one’s nature."

Her figure swayed as she said it, the specific unconscious motion of a being whose basal states were running at this place’s amplified baseline, and Noah looked at the horizon and repeated a mantra in his mind to calm himself and not jump Eon’s dazzling figure.
He stood.

"Everybody wants to be big and strong," he said. "Dominance and power is something every Source will inherently seek here. That is what this place makes plain. And right now we need to keep seeking it."He looked toward the deep vegetation.
"The crabs gave me a picture of the surrounding region. There are Galdr Sources ahead that use Persevere. If I take down four more, I will have the full letter of THE Primordial Tongue."
Eon finished the piece she was eating and came to stand fully beside him.
"We have only just arrived,"she said, "and the one they were looking down on is already making headway fast enough to be the most significant entrant from either House."
She paused.

"I still sense the portion of my existence left behind at the Veiled Causal Site. Sororis Prima Evangelina has been communicating with it. She is coordinating to group the entrants together for better survival odds."Her eyes found his with the expression of a being asking something she was aware is unusual. "What...should I tell her?"
Noah looked at her.

He was her Custos. She was not supposed to be asking him what information to provide to her own people. She was supposed to be directing him. Something had shifted in the hours since they had arrived on this beach together, in the cave, in the dark and the bloom light and the hunting, and the shift had expressed itself as this question, and the question was significant enough that he looked at her for a moment without answering it!

Her expression was open. Her radiant skin caught the bloom light with the warm gold of her Source expression underneath. Her eyes were patient and waiting and completely genuine as...damn, he couldn’t hold back!
He took her lips.

The obsidian Infinity around both of them bounced outward at the contact, their respective Sources reacting to the contact with the enthusiasm of things operating without the filtering their cultivated existence had been maintaining between them, and he did not rush the conclusion of it.
When he finally did let her go, tendrils of Infinity connected from his lips to hers for a moment before dispersing into the ambient air.
Eon breathed out heavily.
"What...was that for? I told you. Emotions here are amplified. You cannot do things like that!"
Her eyes had a fiery light that said something contradictory to the words.
He controlled himself.
"I couldn’t help it." He turned toward the forest. "We will make time for this later. Right now we establish enough power in this region that nothing here can threaten us."
He looked back at her once.
"Tell Evangelina you have been managing the common beasts. You will look for the others when the immediate area is secure."

The Seidr Crabs watched them leave from their line on the dark sand, their claws still for once, their crimson eyes tracking the two figures moving toward the rising vegetation with the attention of beings who had provided information and were now invested in what would happen to the beings they had provided it to.
Noah’s Satiety panel read 97%. Eon had reached 100% somewhere between the Utahraptor’s legs and the present moment.

The forest received them, the massive baobab and banyan formations rising above as the bloom light filtered down through the canopy in shifting golden columns, and the ambient pressure of the deeper terrain pressed against their Sources with the welcome weight of somewhere that took things seriously.
They went in!

chapters.title: Chapter 5255: THE Strand of Broken Scales II
paragraphs: THE Strand of Broken Scales was aptly named.
Noah had traveled enough terrain across enough domains to appreciate when a place had earned its designation rather than been assigned one, and this stretch of coast and ancient forest had earned it.

The rock formations along the waterline had the fractured quality of surfaces that had been subjected to more force than they were built to contain, the breaks clean in some places and jagged in others.

The forest floor was no different. Roots broke through the dark soil in configurations that suggested the growth underneath was competing rather than cooperating, each system pressing against the others for the same limited substrate, the result a terrain that was beautiful and treacherous in the same motion.
He had always liked places like this.
There was an honesty to some places. It asked you to be present, and in return it rewarded the presence.

Eon moved alongside him through the ancient trees with a composure that had resettled after the beach, her golden Source expression stable and close against her figure, her eyes tracking the surrounding growth with focused awareness. She was adapting quickly!

A Silurian Paleozoic entity who had been stripped to her Source and had spent the preceding hours hunting, eating, and navigating the amplified emotional terrain of THE Source Lands without losing her coherence was not doing poorly.
He had also noticed that her figure moved through the forest with a quality this place had no interest in muting.
He redirected his attention to the terrain ahead.

The crabs’ information had been accurate. The Galdr Source pressure ahead had been building against his perception for the last several minutes, the dense obsidian warmth of it distinct from the Seidr Sources scattered through the surrounding forest, and he placed the cluster at approximately half a mile from their current position as their images became visible through the surrounding infinity.
Velociraptors. A group of Seidr ones surrounding a Galdr Source at their center, the arrangement of a predator pack organized around the most powerful member.
His existence got ready.
He had been thinking about long range.

The physical approach had served him well against the Utahraptor. He had no complaints about it. The direct engagement, his hands and feet carrying his Galdr Source through the Infinity-coated strikes, the rolling continuous movement that kept his position unpredictable... it worked, and he liked the directness of it, the confirmation that came with the impact of Source against Source in physical contact.

But he was also a being who had spent considerable time developing expressions of power that operated at distances exceeding arm’s reach, and THE Source Lands had not stripped that preference from him along with his Hadean physiology.
He stopped walking.
Eon stopped beside him without requiring an explanation.

He reached inward and found the reserves of Infinity that had been building through the consumption of the honey badger and the Utahraptor and the cave creature, the Galdr Source density of his expression higher than it had been at arrival in the specific way that it kept being higher than it had been at arrival, each battle and each consumption deepening the viscous concentration of what he was carrying.
He gathered from those reserves with the deliberate attention of a being constructing something that required precision rather than volume.
A singularity.

Not large. The singularity he was constructing was the size of a fist, compressed obsidian Infinity threaded through with the specific expression of his Galdr Source, the two substances combining under the Tongue’s direction into a configuration that held the potential energy of a sustained lightning discharge in the compressed patience of something waiting to be told it could become what it was built to be.
He held it between his palms.
He whispered.
"Sever."
HUUM!

The singularity left his hands at a velocity that the space between his palms and the treeline ahead had no framework for containing, the compressed obsidian Infinity extending into a tendril of lightning that moved through the forest canopy and the obstructing growth and the ambient dark of the spaces between trees.
He began walking.
BOOM!

From the clearing ahead, the sounds arrived. A sharp crack of lightning contact. Then another. Then the cascading sequence of a chain discharge as the first impact propagated its energy laterally to the nearest available Source expressions, which were the Seidr Velociraptors packed around the Galdr at the clearing’s center, each one receiving the chain in the specific sequence of targets that had not seen the attack coming and had therefore not moved.
A chained lightning strike!
The Galdr Source Velociraptor roared.
He heard the earth responding to it, the ground around the clearing rising in sharp formations as the creature’s Source expression drove into the surrounding terrain to form a barrier!
The lightning pierced through.

He heard Persevere. Then Persevere again. Then again, the roar containing less each time, the Primordial Tongue’s letter arriving from a smaller reserve with each successive use, the specific diminishing quality of a word being spent faster than it was replenishing.
By the time he and Eon reached the clearing, the scene had finished resolving itself.

Scorched Seidr Velociraptors were scattered across the clearing floor in the still configurations. The earth formations the Galdr Source had raised stood as misshapen evidence of a defense that had not been sufficient.
At the center, the Galdr Source Velociraptor itself was on the ground, its body trembling!
Its eyes found Noah as he walked into the clearing, and what was in those eyes was hatred in the pure unfiltered form this place amplified to its maximum expression.
Noah crouched in front of it.
He looked at it for a moment.
He raised his hand and slashed sideways!
HUUM!
The motion was clean and final.
"Existence is unfair." He held the creature’s gaze until the light left it. "Apologies."
HUUM!
The fragment rose from the Galdr Source Velociraptor’s broken expression, obsidian and faintly luminous, drifting upward with the patient certainty of something that knew it was being claimed.
|Second Fragment of the Letter Persevere obtained. Two of five.|

|The Galdr Velociraptor used Persevere three times before collapse. First Utahraptor required four cycles. Either your Sever expression is more efficient than your physical approach, or this individual had a shallower reserve to draw from.|
|Satiety status: 97%. The surrounding Seidr Velociraptors represent approximately 8% recovery each. The Galdr Source body will provide significantly more.|
Noah straightened and looked at the available consumption around him.
He looked at Eon.
"Eat." He gestured at the surrounding scorched Seidr Velociraptors. "Take your time with it."
He looked at the Galdr Source body at the clearing’s center and then back at her.
"That one is yours."
She looked at him and nodded lightly.

Ge sat against one of the earth formations the creature had raised and began his own consumption from the nearest Seidr body."A Galdr Source consumed in full will help you attain Galdr Source quicker..."
He watched her process this.

She moved toward the Galdr Source Velociraptor body without further comment, and Noah returned to his own consumption, and the clearing was quiet except for the sounds of two existences doing what THE Source Lands required of them.
He smiled as he looked at Eon.
One had to treat their woman well.
This remained true regardless of which iteration of existence one was currently inhabiting, and Noah had never found reason to argue with it!

chapters.title: Chapter 5256: THE Strand of Broken Scales! III
paragraphs: A part of him walked across THE Source Lands.
The rest of him had not stopped moving.
This was the nature of the distributed existence he had built, a thing he had once found remarkable and had since come to regard as simply the way things were.
One body hunted with Eon through ancient Land while other bodies did what other bodies did, each one carrying enough of him to act without requiring instruction from the whole.

He was accustomed to the sensation by now the simultaneous awareness of several operational contexts, each running at full presence, none of them diminished by the others. Most beings found this concept difficult to hold. He found it convenient and glorious!
Across THE Wandering Territories and beyond, the Apeiron were moving.

They had taken to the task the way his people had always taken to tasks he set them: with the thoroughness of beings who understood that the alternative to succeeding was unacceptable. They knew they needed adversity!

The scattered Gilded Ones, displaced by his Directives to the most inhospitable coordinates Observable Existence offered, had found themselves in Transcendent Folds and Dead Wheels of Existence and stranger territories still. Some had ended up in THE Lands of the Dead, which Noah found darkly appropriate and did not dwell on further.
In a shattered remnant of THE Loom, a group had formed around Ul’moreth, THE Big Stepper.
He was still hairy.

This was the thing about Ul’moreth’s Apeiron form that distinguished it from every other Apeiron Noah had seen. Every other member of his people had accepted the scale architecture, the dorsal protrusions, the clean draconic musculature that the engineering produced. Ul’moreth had received all of these and had additionally received, through whatever the engineering had decided was appropriate for his specific foundation, an extraordinary quantity of thick blue-gold hair covering his massive frame from shoulders to ankles.

He had reportedly attempted to be free of it in the early minutes of his transformation, and had reportedly reached the conclusion that being free of it felt wrong in a way that was difficult to explain.
He had remained hairy.
He floated now at the center of a hunting group with the patient readiness of a being who had made peace with his appearance and was prepared to direct his attention toward other matters.

Beside him, Skoll, the very good boy, occupied the sky in the form he had arrived at through the Apeiron engineering, which was the form of a wolf that had decided the word massive needed a new definition and had provided one!

THE Emperor Penguin was present, compact and deliberate, its Source burns from the earlier collapse long since processed through its recovery cycle. THE Fisherman floated quietly at the group’s perimeter, which was where THE Fisherman tended to float.
Lumivara burned with a cold silver luminescence, which in the Apeiron form had become a silver luminescence that reminded observers of something that was also very large and very dangerous.

Groups like this were moving throughout the scattered displacement zones, Apeiron hunting in formations because the individual Gilded Ones, even stripped of Infinity by his Directives, remained more than any single Apeiron was built to address alone. The strategy was sound. His people understood it and were executing it with the discipline of beings who had been trained well and trusted the training!
As for Noah himself.

His Primus Apeiron form floated inside a Collapsed Transcendent Conceptual Fold. The fold had collapsed inward across whatever conceptual framework had sustained it, existence curving in on the abstract concepts the space had been organized around, reality layering through ideas rather than through geography. It should have been deeply disorienting as Noah merely found it interesting.

The multicolored deluge that had flooded through the fold burned across every surface the space offered, the Infinity finding the abstract contours of a conceptual space and expressing itself through them in ways that were visually extraordinary.
He was emanating...brilliance currently.

That was the word for what was happening through his Primus Apeiron form. The Galdr Source he was developing in THE Source Lands through one body was doing something across all his bodies simultaneously, a resonance between his Source at its most fundamental and the Primus Apeiron form that was his most refined external expression.

The obsidian multicolored glow of the Galdr Source was pressing outward through the Apeiron scales in a way that compounded with the scales’ existing Infinity expression rather than conflicting with it.

He felt compressed to his most true values. That was the sensation. Everything external stripped back to its irreducible core, even here where he had most of his external components intact, the Galdr Source insisting on the truth beneath the architecture.

His Infinite Scales had always been a framework he was pioneering as he went, adding to and restructuring as new knowledge arrived. The Primordial Source, the letters of THE Primordial Tongue, the Source Demarcation system...all of it was suggesting a deeper layer of the framework than he had built to yet. If he incorporated Source at its truest expression into his Infinite Scales, and then eventually, through the adversity of THE Source Lands, accessed THE Primordial Source itself, the resulting Scales would be something he did not have complete vocabulary for yet!
He was looking forward to finding it out!

Ragnar V49 was approximately forty meters ahead of him, separated by a stretch of curved conceptual reality that the fold had bent into something resembling a corridor made of collapsed ideas. The brutal smile was present. It was always present. Noah had come to regard it as a fixed feature of the environment wherever a Ragnar appeared, like the ground or the dark.
"You ready, big guy?"
Ragnar’s expression did not change.
"Yeah, buddy boy, I’m ready." He cracked his neck.
"I hope you are also ready for how this Observable Existence is about to be turned into barren wastelands.Haha. I hope you are ready!"
BOOM!
Noah’s eyes went cold.
The Galdr Source blazed through every scale of his Primus Apeiron form simultaneously, the obsidian multicolored brilliance building in the fraction of an instant before the fraction concluded.
He shot forward!
BOOM!

chapters.title: Chapter 5257: Overcome All Adversity! I
paragraphs: There was a danger in accomplishment that most beings never examined because the examining required unflinching honesty that accomplishment itself tended to make difficult.

The danger was perception. When something grand was achieved, the mind reached for a category large enough to hold it, and the categories it reached for were often too large. An accomplishment perceived as unfathomable became a destination rather than a waypoint, and destinations ended journeys.

A being who had climbed to a peak they considered the ultimate peak had no reason to look for the next one, and if they had no reason to look for the next one, the next one would not be found, and the one after that would not be found, and the vast architecture of what they might have become would remain unbuilt because they had mistaken a single floor for the whole structure.

The correct relationship to accomplishment was simpler and considerably harder to maintain. Each achievement was a point in an endless journey. Significant because all points in a worthy journey were significant. No more significant than the next point, which had not arrived yet, and would be grander.
This was the only way to keep moving. To look at something genuinely extraordinary and think: good. What comes next?
Noah had been practicing this relationship for longer than he would have consciously admitted!

He stood at the crown of a wide ancient tree whose upper canopy broke above the surrounding forest canopy into open bloom light, and what occupied the massive nest at the tree’s highest platform of branches was extremely unhappy with his presence.

The flying dinosaur had a wingspan that covered the nest platform’s full diameter with room to spare, its body long and scaled in the specific dark iridescence of creatures that spent their existence above everything else and had developed the aesthetics of altitude.

A Galdr Source, the densest he had encountered in THE Strand of Broken Scales since the Utahraptor, its Source expression blazing with the bright chaotic warmth of a being defending something it considered inviolable. The nest around it was layered infinity and accumulated Source energy compressed into the architecture of a home rather than a weapon, and the creature was currently deploying both as weapons with the indiscriminate thoroughness.
Noah directed the storm.

He had been building it before the creature realized the storm was directed, gathering the obsidian Infinity that saturated the upper air of THE Strand into the swirling formation of a lightning system rather than a collection of individual strikes, and the system was making no accommodations for the nest or its occupant.

The multicolored current within the lightning carried his Galdr Source through every discharge, each bolt carrying Source against Source impact at the contact point rather than simple electrical force.
The Galdr Source beast persevered twice!

The second Persevere came from a reserve that had been significantly depleted by the first, and what it healed was less than what the storm had taken, and the storm continued. The creature fought with the full extraordinary capability of something that had survived by being the apex of its particular environment for years, its lightning capabilities and its superior aerial mobility and its territorial fury all expressed at maximum.
The storm was broader than all three!
When the Galdr Source beast collapsed, it collapsed with finality.
Eon arrived at the tree’s upper branches as the storm dissipated, her golden Source expression bright and her eyes brighter, the expectation in them visible before she spoke.

"This will be the fifth one."She looked at what remained of the nest and the creature with the calculating attention of someone who had spent the last hour developing a working knowledge of what five Galdr Source defeats meant.
"With it, we can finally make headway into grasping something about THE Primordial Source."
Noah nodded.

Five. In whatever passed for an hour in THE Source Lands, where time was not a factor his body recognized but his awareness still tracked through the accumulated weight of events, they had moved through five Galdr Source creatures that wielded a letter of THE Primordial Tongue. The hunting had been excellent. He was not going to say this out loud, but the hunting had been genuinely excellent!
He raised his hand.

The fifth fragment rose from the creature’s broken Source and drifted toward him without requiring the summoning, the obsidian light of it moving with the patient certainty of something arriving at its destination.

The other four fragments answered from wherever they had been resting within his Source expression, coming forward to meet the fifth, and the five pieces of the letter of Persevere began rotating around him in slow orbit.
The rotation accelerated.

The obsidian light between the five fragments intensified as they moved, the pieces recognizing each other and completing the connection between them, and then the acceleration reached its conclusion and the pieces merged.

A blinding beam of obsidian light shot upward from the convergence point into the bloom-lit sky above the canopy, the signal of a completed thing announcing itself to whatever this place used for an observer. Noah frowned at it briefly. Whatever attention it drew, it drew. He had not been operating with subtlety as a primary consideration.
He looked at what the five fragments had become.

A...letter. Ancient in the way that things were ancient when they had existed before the frameworks used to measure age had been established, its form carrying the specific geometry of a language that did not use an alphabet any surviving writing system had derived from. It communicated toward him as it rotated, the letter actively oriented toward his Source expression rather than passively existing in the air between them.
As if it had been waiting to be completed.
As if it had been waiting for him specifically.
It surged forward and entered him.

The comprehension arrived not as information but as recognition, the understanding settling into his Source at the foundational level rather than the cognitive one, the letter becoming a thing he knew the way he knew his own name rather than a thing he had learned.
Persevere.
Through boundless adversity, persevere. Through all the unfairness of existence, persevere. Through the weight of every force that pressed against what you were trying to build, persevere!
Through the moments when the calculation said the odds were unacceptable and the moment demanded you act anyway, persevere. So long as you persevered, everything would be okay!
Not a promise. A principle. The first and most fundamental letter of THE Primordial Tongue, the language of THE Primordial Source, and it was the one that said: continue.
For the first time, Noah opened his mouth.
"Persevere!"
BOOM!

A blinding beam of obsidian light shot upward from the convergence point into the bloom-lit sky above the canopy, the signal of a completed thing announcing itself to whatever this place used for an observer.
Noah frowned at it briefly.
Whatever attention it drew, it drew.
He had not been operating with subtlety as a primary consideration.
He looked at what the five fragments had become.
A...letter.

Ancient in the way that things were ancient when they had existed before the frameworks used to measure age had been established, its form carrying the specific geometry of a language that did not use an alphabet any surviving writing system had derived from.
It communicated toward him as it rotated, the letter actively oriented toward his Source expression rather than passively existing in the air between them.
As if it had been waiting to be completed.
As if it had been waiting for him specifically.
It surged forward and entered him.

The comprehension arrived not as information but as recognition, the understanding settling into his Source at the foundational level rather than the cognitive one, the letter becoming a thing he knew the way he knew his own name rather than a thing he had learned.
Persevere.
Through boundless adversity, persevere.
Through all the unfairness of existence, persevere.
Through the weight of every force that pressed against what you were trying to build, persevere!
Through the moments when the calculation said the odds were unacceptable and the moment demanded you act anyway, persevere.
So long as you persevered, everything would be okay!
Not a promise.
A principle.
The first and most fundamental letter of THE Primordial Tongue, the language of THE Primordial Source, and it was the one that said: continue.
For the first time, Noah opened his mouth.
"Persevere!"
BOOM!

chapters.title: Chapter 5258: Overcome All Adversity! II
paragraphs: Multicolored flames erupted from him in incandescent billowing waves that had no interest in being contained by the tree’s canopy or the surrounding air or any other intervening medium!

They came from the core of him, from his Galdr Source, from his Infinity, from everything that could accurately be called himself, and they burned through his existence not as destruction but as its opposite.

Any injury to his Source healed. Any fatigue dissolved. Any weakness in his foundations reinforced itself from the inside out, the flames finding the places that had given under the sustained hunting of the past hour and restoring them to something better than they had been before the hunting had found them. His existence was one step stronger. The step was real, measurable, and had cost him nothing except the utterance.
Oh!
This was the thing!
|THE Primordial Tongue- First Letter Accessed: Persevere.|

|Connection to THE Primordial Source established at foundational level. Access at this stage is limited to the letter Persevere and the capabilities it carries. Further letters require further development.|

|Quantified effects of Persevere: Immediate restoration of Source injuries upon utterance. Immediate dissolution of accumulated fatigue. Reinforcement of current foundational strength to a state exceeding the pre-utterance baseline.No ceiling on the reinforcement effect has been identified, the letter appears to scale with the strength of the Source uttering it.|

|Standard cost: Persevere draws from the Source of the being uttering it. The letter empowers while depleting. For the Galdr Source creatures you defeated, this produced a diminishing cycle, each utterance empowered them while depleting the reserve needed for the next utterance, until the reserve was insufficient to sustain another cycle.|
|Error logged. Reclassifying as basal function.|

|The latent weavings of THE Cheating Architect, THE Protagonist, and Perpetual Harvest are deeply entrenched within your Source. They have excluded themselves from the cost calculation of Persevere, which means they have excluded everything in your existence that connects to them.The Source cost of uttering Persevere has been redirected away from most other things comprising your Source.|
|What remains to pay the cost is your Infinity.|
|Your Infinity will pay the cost of a letter that heals you, reinforces you, and elevates your foundational strength beyond its prior state.|
|Infinity pays for your perseverance.|
BOOM!

Noah’s body shook from the full-body response of a being receiving information that reorganized the significance of everything around it simultaneously. His Primus Apeiron form across the Collapsed Transcendent Conceptual Fold was burning with the same recognition at the same moment. Every body he occupied shook, briefly, in unison!
Haha, what?
WHAT?!

He had watched Galdr Source beasts deploy Persevere and diminish with each usage, the cost depleting the very reserve the letter was supposed to protect, the tragedy of it being the diminishing return embedded in the mechanism. He had factored this into his understanding of what gaining Persevere would mean for him.
He had not factored his most unique weavings deciding they had opinions about the matter.
His cost was Infinity.
Fucking Infinity!
Eon came toward him across the canopy branch with urgency, her expression carrying the worry of someone who had watched a being they were invested in physically shake without obvious cause.

He was laughing! The private laugh of a being who had just confirmed something about themselves that they had suspected across a very long climb and had now received empirical validation of, the laugh that came from genuine amusement rather than performance.
He looked at her.
"I’m fine,"he said. "I’m very fine."
He looked at his hands, still burning faintly with the residual multicolored flames of the first utterance.
He had always paid for everything with Infinity.
Why would THE Primordial Tongue be different?
Some moments in a journey were simply different from the others.

He had learned to recognize them without inflating them, because inflation was the enemy of continued movement, and continued movement was the only thing that produced the next moment. But recognition was not inflation. A being who could not identify when something genuinely significant had happened was as lost as a being who could not move past the significance once identified.

Infinity had always been the foundation. The number one factor that allowed him to outclass existences who had been alive for millions or billions of years, who had cultivated across spans of time that made his own span look like an afternoon. They had time. He had Infinity in quantities and expressions that their cultivated frameworks had never produced, and the gap between those two resources, in practice, had always resolved in his favor!

The Infiniverse was the second factor. A floating land mass blooming into an Observable Existence, Primordial Realms pushing upward through its substrate, Miniature Infinite Causes accelerating its development toward something that would rival the arrangements that had taken eons to produce. Nobody else had this. Nobody else had conceived of it!

It existed because he had looked at what was available to him and decided to make something that had not existed before, which was, when he examined the pattern honestly, how most of his significant capabilities had arrived.
There had been moments in the climb that steered everything afterward. Each one had opened a territory that the territory preceding it had not made visible.
Touching a component of THE Primordial Source, which at this moment meant a single letter of THE Primordial Tongue, felt like one of those moments.

Not because of what Persevere itself could do, though what it could do was not small. Because of the cost. Because the power had a cost, and his existence had looked at the cost and redirected it to something literally infinite, and what that implied about the relationship between his existence and THE Primordial Tongue had not yet finished revealing itself.
He wanted to find out how far the implication extended.
"Persevere."

The multicolored flames rose again, billowing outward from his Galdr Source through his existence with the comprehensive warmth of a letter doing exactly what it had been designed to do. Every surface of what he was reinforced itself, the elevation real and immediate.
|Persevere- Second Utterance.|

|Foundation: elevated. The reinforcement compounds on the previous utterance’s baseline rather than returning to the pre-first-utterance state. Each successive utterance elevates from the most recently elevated position.|
|Infinity: cost paid. Reserves reduced by a fraction that remains negligible relative to current density.|
|Observable Force: minor elevation registered. The letter appears to affect the full composition of the Galdr Source rather than the Source substrate alone.|
|Galdr Source expression: denser than one second ago.|

chapters.title: Chapter 5259: Overcome All Adversity! III
paragraphs: Noah’s smile was growing.
One second.
"Persevere!"

The old flames had not finished settling before new ones rose to replace them, the second utterance’s billowing warmth overlapping with the first’s residual heat, the nest around him blazing with the compound expression of a letter being used by someone who had confirmed there was no cost to using it and had drawn the logical conclusion about what to do with that confirmation.
|Persevere- Third Utterance.|
|Foundation: elevated from second utterance baseline. The compound reinforcement is measurable. Continued utterance will produce continued elevation with no identified ceiling thus far.|
|Infinity: cost paid. The fraction paid per utterance remains consistent. At current Infinity density, the sustainable utterance rate is effectively unlimited.|
He was almost laughing.
Almost. The tyrannical composure held the almost in place, but only barely, the amusement pressing against it from the inside with more force than it usually pressed!

The Galdr Source beasts he had hunted through THE Strand of Broken Scales had each deployed Persevere across cycles of diminishing return, the letter spending them as it empowered them, the tragedy built into the mechanism. He had watched them become stronger, the empowerment real and the depletion equally real.
He was paying with Infinity.
"Persevere!"

Again. The flames were continuous now, the utterances close enough together that the rise and fall between them had become a single sustained expression, the nest and the ancient tree and the surrounding canopy all bathed in the multicolored light of a man confirming something about himself that he found deeply satisfying.
Eon was watching with shining eyes.

She knew the word. He could see that she knew it in the expression she wore, the specific recognition of a being who had encountered the word in another context and was now watching it emerge from someone she had not expected to possess it. The word the Relictus uttered. The word that those who had access to THE Primordial Source reached for when their existence required something from the deepest available layer of what they were.

Something the Gilded Ones had been reaching toward for many Ages...veginning to fall within his grasp in THE Strand of Broken Scales, on top of a flying dinosaur’s nest, within an hour of his arrival.

"You may want to slow down."She said it with the measured concern of someone who had observed a pattern and drawn a reasonable conclusion from it. "You don’t want to exhaust your Source by using that letter every time you feel like it."
She had no idea.

He looked at her face in the light of the continuous multicolored flames, at the genuine worry behind the reasonable concern, at the innocence of a being who had watched the Galdr Source beasts spend themselves on that word and had reasonably assumed the same mechanism applied here.

He had been managing the amplified emotional environment of THE Source Lands with discipline, which was the correct approach and which he had maintained because the correct approach mattered. But he had also, in the same period, integrated a Primordial Tongue letter, survived the Advent Wall crossing, hunted five Galdr Source beasts, and confirmed that THE Primordial Tongue cost him Infinity.
Discipline had limits. The appropriate response to an event of this magnitude was celebration, and celebration could not be indefinitely deferred.
He moved toward her.

Eon saw him coming through the continuous multicolored flames wreathing his figure, saw his eyes, and her Source did something her composure noted and did not entirely manage to suppress. Something in her expression that had been composed shifted toward attentive.

His flaming hands found her face with a gentleness that the flames did not contradict, the multicolored warmth of Persevere’s continuous utterance pressing softly against her cheek as he held her and looked at her with the calm unhurried attention of a being who had decided where he was and had no interest in being anywhere else.
"Persevere," he said.
BOOM!
She would need to as this time, he would not be stopping at having her lips.

The multicolored flames expanded outward and rose and covered the nest in every direction, obscuring the upper canopy, the bloom light, the surrounding trees, and any possible line of sight from anything that might have been watching a man celebrate the beginning of something terrifying.
<Ubergulden Dietrich>
THE Source Lands had opinions about pride.

Dietrich had formed this assessment rather quickly into his crossing of THE Advent Wall, when the stripping had begun and the thing that remained had discovered that the thing that remained was not substantially diminished by the stripping.
But right now...

He was bleeding from three locations that mattered and several that did not, his Custodes Mira moving beside him with her left arm held against her body in the careful way of someone who had made peace with a temporary limitation and was reserving their attention for more immediate concerns.

They had ran away from and survived the first Galdr Source beast encounter through the combination of his Source expression and her strategic instincts, and the second encounter through sheer refusal, and the third had left them both in the state they were currently navigating.
The deep forest of THE Strand of Broken Scales had no interest in his House’s name.
He was reconsidering this when the three figures emerged from the tree line ahead.

All three of them wore scars, the marks of engagements this place had required of them distributed across their arms and shoulders and the planes of their faces with the specificity of a history that was still being accumulated.
Their Sources burned with the steady warmth of beings who had been here long enough to find their footing and had not spent that time resting. Their eyes were bright!
Dietrich recognized all three of them at once and felt something in his chest that was, in fact, relief.
"Sororis Prima Lana."He stepped forward and did not try to make his voice smaller than it was. "Ubergulden Shatta. Ubergulden Riyanna."
He looked at each face in sequence and found each face exactly as he had hoped to find it. "I have never been happier to see faces like yours in this forsaken place."

Ubergulden Shatta raised a hand in the gesture of someone about to say something that required a quieter delivery than the greeting had used. He was broad across the shoulders, his golden hair worn loose, his Source expression carrying the denser warmth of an existence that had been feeding well.

"Now, now. Keep the volume down." The amusement in his voice was genuine and not unkind. "The more of us together, the better, and strength in numbers has mattered in very few places as much as it matters here."
He looked past Dietrich briefly, assessing.
"We were told others entered this time and to come to the periphery of the strand and find you. You didn’t manage to locate any of them? Are they still alive?"

chapters.title: Chapter 5260: Overcome All Adversity! IV
paragraphs: Dietrich’s face went through a change he did not fully control.
"My sister has no protector." He said it with the flatness of a fact that had been pressing against the back of his thoughts since the crossing.
"Who knows what she is currently going through. If you are all intact enough, could we search the periphery for her before returning? Even an hour of looking-"
Sororis Prima Lana’s interjected.

"We can continue searching for a few more hours," she said, carefully. "But you do not want to be in these forests when the Illumination Flowers fade. The dark here is not merely dark. The Galdr Source creatures that move through it are different from what you have encountered in the bloom period. We need enough time to return to camp before it fades."

She met his eyes with the directness of someone who was not softening what she was saying. "Communicate with your sister through the thread you left at THE Advent Wall. If Sororis Prima Evangelina outside the Wall can relay what your sister sees around her, any landmarks she can identify, we may be able to narrow the search considerably."
Dietrich reached for the thread.

The sliver of his existence left behind outside THE Advent Wall was present, and communicating through it was a sensation of speaking across a limitation that was not distance but something more structural than distance. He pressed his intent through the connection toward Evangelina and held the channel while he waited for information to return.
What returned was not his sister’s voice.

Evangelina’s reply came back measured and clipped. Adelheid’s golden thread outside the Wall showed her alive. The thread was active. The existence it was connected to continued. But the thread was not responding to communication, not because it was severed but because the existence on the other end of it was occupied with something that was consuming its full attention.
She might be fighting for her life.

He had argued against her coming. He had not argued hard enough. He had looked at the Custos arrangement she had arrived with, the Luxuria standing behind her with the infuriating calm of something that did not understand its own insignificance, and he had found the arrangement unworthy and had said so!
Yet...ah!
He blamed himself for allowing it.
He blamed the Luxuria for existing in a position where being allowed was a meaningful variable.
"She is not responding,"he said to Sororis Prima Lana.
"Then we look." He met Lana’s eyes. "However many hours we have before the dark, we look."
Mira, who had been quiet since the three Ubergulden emerged from the treeline, shifted her weight off her compromised arm and back into the readiness of a Custodes with somewhere to be.
Dietrich moved, and his Custodes moved with him, and the three scarred Gilded Ones moved alongside them, and the deep forest of THE Strand of Broken Scales received them all!
THE Strand did not care about their House name!

Away from THE Source Lands, in a Collapsed Transcendent Conceptual Fold where existence curved through abstract concepts that the collapse had compressed into visible geometry, Noah floated in his Primus Apeiron form and looked up at Ragnar V49.
The battle had been going on long enough that its texture had changed.

The first exchange had been an assessment. The second had been a confirmation of the assessment. What they were doing now was something else, the specific sustained pressure of two beings who had found each other’s level and were testing whether either of them had a level above the one they were currently occupying!
Ragnar was laughing.
"Buddy boy." He shook his head, the brutal smile wider than usual. "We seem evenly matched. Which is shocking in itself, because I was pummeling you not long ago."

He tilted his head with the assessment of a being who had been doing this for a very long time. "But here’s the thing. The longer this goes, the sooner a truly resounding force gets sent down to address whatever is happening here. You are getting stronger as time passes."
His confidence settled into something absolute. "But it will not be significant enough. It will not."
He said it without malice.
He said it the way someone stated the position of a mountain!

Noah looked at his clawed hand. The Galdr Source emanating through his Primus Apeiron scales had deepened across the duration of this battle, the additional density from the Persevere utterances in THE Source Lands pressing through the connection between his bodies with the compound warmth of something growing faster than the battle was expecting it to grow.
He looked up at Ragnar.
"Then all I will have to do,"he said, "is Persevere."
BOOM!

Multicolored flames erupted from him in billowing continuous waves, the letter answering the utterance as it had answered every utterance since he had first grasped it in THE Strand of Broken Scales. They came from the deepest available layer of what he was. Not from his Infinity. Not from his Galdr Source alone. From something beneath both of those, the foundational layer that THE Primordial Source touched and that THE Primordial Tongue expressed, and what came from that layer carried a quality that Infinity-only expressions did not carry.
His Primus Apeiron form stood inside the flames with the easy composure of something that had always belonged there!

The multicolored scales caught the flame and refracted it through their prismatic surfaces until the figure at the center of the conflagration was difficult to resolve as a distinct shape and easy to resolve as a single blazing fact. His four horns burned at their singularity tips. His crown spun above his head with the additional fire layered through its orbit!
The dorsal protrusions along his back channeled the flame’s warmth through the Observable Force lines between them in visible golden rivers.
His gaze was imperious.
He directed his existence!
Utilize Persevere continuously. Do not stop.
|Persevere- Continuous Utilization Protocol established.|

|Current limitation: The letter of THE Primordial Tongue can be expressed once per second at the foundational level of your current access. This limitation is not yours specifically, it is a function of the letter itself and of THE Primordial Tongue’s architecture more broadly. The Tongue operates at a cadence that exceeds ordinary existential expression but is not without constraint. One utterance per second represents the current maximum frequency for this letter at your access level.|

|Each utterance elevates from the previous utterance’s baseline. Compound elevation is active. Continuous utilization will produce continuous elevation at one-second intervals for as long as the protocol is maintained.|
|Infinity cost per utterance: negligible relative to current infinity. Sustained utilization is viable.|
|Beginning.|
The flames did not stop.

They rose and rose and rose in the one-second rhythm of a letter being spoken continuously into the foundation of an existence that had no cost to speak it, each wave overlapping the trailing edge of the previous one, the compound elevation accumulating in the specific way that things accumulated when they were building on their own prior state rather than returning to a fixed baseline between iterations.

Ragnar’s expression changed.The smile held. But behind it, something recalibrated with the speed of a being who had encountered this phenomenon before, who had a classification for what this quality of flame meant, and who had not expected to find that classification applicable to whatever Noah was.
"You were connected to THE Relictus?"He stared. The incredulity was genuine. "You should have shown that earlier. The full force of THE Gilded Ones would have come down for you."He laughed!
"Haha, wow. This is crazy!" His eyes found Noah’s.
"Okay, buddy boy."The brutal smile became something that held respect in it alongside everything else it held. "You are about to be famous."
He shot forward.
BOOM!

The distance between them collapsed in the interval that characterized Ragnar’s closing speed, the Cause-backed force behind his approach cracking the curved conceptual geometry of the Collapsed Fold around the path he traveled. Noah watched him come with the focused calm of someone who had been tracking this approach since before it began.
He punched.

The full compound weight of what the continuous Persevere utterances had built across the preceding seconds behind the strike, his Primus Apeiron fist driving into the center of Ragnar’s chest at the moment the distance between them reached contact range.
The Infinity behind it came through his Source and THE Infinite Tongue simultaneously, the Tongue speaking the impact into Ragnar’s foundations rather than against his exterior.
The dent appeared.
Then the cracks, spreading outward from the impact point across Ragnar’s Silurian-tier chest!
The cracks were real! They were the record of something that had found a gap in what Ragnar V49 was built to withstand.
BOOM!
Ragnar went backward like a cannonball.

The Collapsed Transcendent Conceptual Fold received him at the far edge of the space, the curved conceptual geometry buckling around the impact of a Silurian Paleozoic Ira Gilded One being sent through it at a velocity he had not generated himself, and for a moment the laughing stopped.
Noah floated in the continuous multicolored flames and watched.
The flames kept rising.
One Persevere per second!
One! Per! Second!

"My sister has no protector." He said it with the flatness of a fact that had been pressing against the back of his thoughts since the crossing.
"Who knows what she is currently going through.
If you are all intact enough, could we search the periphery for her before returning?
Even an hour of looking-"
Sororis Prima Lana’s interjected.
"We can continue searching for a few more hours," she said, carefully.
"But you do not want to be in these forests when the Illumination Flowers fade.
The dark here is not merely dark.
The Galdr Source creatures that move through it are different from what you have encountered in the bloom period.
We need enough time to return to camp before it fades."
She met his eyes with the directness of someone who was not softening what she was saying.
"Communicate with your sister through the thread you left at THE Advent Wall.
If Sororis Prima Evangelina outside the Wall can relay what your sister sees around her, any landmarks she can identify, we may be able to narrow the search considerably."
Dietrich reached for the thread.

The sliver of his existence left behind outside THE Advent Wall was present, and communicating through it was a sensation of speaking across a limitation that was not distance but something more structural than distance.
He pressed his intent through the connection toward Evangelina and held the channel while he waited for information to return.
What returned was not his sister’s voice.
Evangelina’s reply came back measured and clipped.
Adelheid’s golden thread outside the Wall showed her alive.
The thread was active.
The existence it was connected to continued.
But the thread was not responding to communication, not because it was severed but because the existence on the other end of it was occupied with something that was consuming its full attention.
She might be fighting for her life.
He had argued against her coming.
He had not argued hard enough.

He had looked at the Custos arrangement she had arrived with, the Luxuria standing behind her with the infuriating calm of something that did not understand its own insignificance, and he had found the arrangement unworthy and had said so!
Yet...ah!
He blamed himself for allowing it.
He blamed the Luxuria for existing in a position where being allowed was a meaningful variable.
"She is not responding,"he said to Sororis Prima Lana.
"Then we look." He met Lana’s eyes.
"However many hours we have before the dark, we look."
Mira, who had been quiet since the three Ubergulden emerged from the treeline, shifted her weight off her compromised arm and back into the readiness of a Custodes with somewhere to be.

The first exchange had been an assessment.
The second had been a confirmation of the assessment.

What they were doing now was something else, the specific sustained pressure of two beings who had found each other’s level and were testing whether either of them had a level above the one they were currently occupying!
Ragnar was laughing.
"Buddy boy." He shook his head, the brutal smile wider than usual.
"We seem evenly matched.
Which is shocking in itself, because I was pummeling you not long ago."

"But here’s the thing.
The longer this goes, the sooner a truly resounding force gets sent down to address whatever is happening here.
You are getting stronger as time passes."
His confidence settled into something absolute.
"But it will not be significant enough.
It will not."
He said it without malice.
He said it the way someone stated the position of a mountain!
Noah looked at his clawed hand.

The Galdr Source emanating through his Primus Apeiron scales had deepened across the duration of this battle, the additional density from the Persevere utterances in THE Source Lands pressing through the connection between his bodies with the compound warmth of something growing faster than the battle was expecting it to grow.

chapters.title: Chapter 5261: Quintessential Immensity! I
paragraphs: Ragnar V49 hit the far wall of the Collapsed Transcendent Conceptual Fold and came off it grinning.
The cracks in his chest were real. He looked at them with the appreciation of someone who had not seen cracks in his chest in a very long time and found the novelty interesting!

"Okay." He rolled his neck. THE Dominion Cause blazed through his left hand and THE Bellum Cause through his right, both Prime Cause integrations burning at full expression, the compound authority of two integrated truths pressing outward through his frame and into the surrounding space.
The conceptual geometry of the Fold bent around the pressure of it. "Now we’re talking. We! Are! Talking!"
He drove both hands together.

The resulting surge hit Noah across the full width of the Fold simultaneously, THE Dominion Cause asserting the hierarchy of the space and THE Bellum Cause feeding violence into every coordinate the assertion touched. The combined expression filled the Fold from wall to wall.
Noah was already redirecting it.

THE Infinite Vector caught the leading edge and adjusted the direction- not fully, not yet, the magnitude of two integrated Prime Causes pushing against the Vector’s current capacity and finding partial purchase. The surge hit Noah at roughly a third of its full force. He took it, absorbed it, and was already moving by the time Ragnar processed that the attack hadn’t landed cleanly!
Every second, the flames rose.

Persevere stacked on Persevere and the compound elevation built in Noah’s Galdr Source, the Primordial flames burning through his Primus Apeiron form in denser waves with each iteration, his scales pulling the warmth into their prismatic surfaces and compressing it into the foundation of what he was rather than letting it disperse outward.

His Hadean Pillar of Infinity, his Civilizations, his Infinity... all of it ran through the Galdr Source now as a conduit rather than as separate systems, the Source sitting beneath all of them and amplifying everything that moved through it.
Ragnar came in hard, low, fast!

The Bellum Cause erupted from his body in a close-range expression that turned his skin into a weapon, and he drove that weapon at Noah’s torso with the full committed weight of a Silurian Paleozoic Ira Gilded One who had finally decided to stop feeling out his opponent.
Noah stepped into it and hit him three times in the span of one step.

Ragnar absorbed two and the third found the cracks in his chest from the cannonball strike earlier, the impact driving into the compromised architecture and spreading the damage outward. He disengaged with a laugh!
"You’re not fighting like a man anymore, buddy boy!"

He raised both hands, THE Dominion Cause and THE Bellum Cause surging together, and drove them into the floor of the Fold. The conceptual geometry fractured beneath the strike, abstract concepts cracking open and releasing their compressed meanings into the air as distorted light.
"Let me remind you what full Prime Cause expression looks like!"
The Fold shook.
Noah watched the shaking with cold eyes and reached for Ragnar’s momentum.

THE Infinite Vector found it. Ragnar’s forward drive, the kinetic commitment of his next approach, the directional investment of a being charging with full Cause backing behind the charge. The Vector rewrote the direction by twenty degrees. Ragnar’s charge carried him past Noah’s left side instead of through his center.
The flames kept rising!

Every second, denser. Every second, the Galdr Source pressed deeper into his Primus Apeiron foundations, the compound elevation building toward something the Fold’s space was starting to register as a pressure it hadn’t been designed to contain. The multicolored obsidian fire wasn’t dispersing anymore. It was accumulating around him in dense slow-churning waves that pressed outward against the curved walls of the conceptual space!
He reached for Ragnar’s momentum again.
This time it moved the way he wanted it to move.
He had grown stronger to be able to!

The Vector caught the direction of Ragnar’s positioning and redirected it fully, and Ragnar went sideways instead of backward, the Silurian Paleozoic frame moving without generating the movement, the Cause expression burning through his body failing to override the Vector’s grip on the direction the Infinity within his bones was now traveling!
"What!"
Noah pulled.

Ragnar came toward him at speed, his mass not fighting the pull so much as discovering the pull had already made the relevant decision, and Noah hit him twice mid-approach before the approach concluded. Both strikes found the chest cracks. Both went deeper!
BOOM!
"Buddy boy, this isn’t-"
Noah waved his hand.

Ragnar swung sideways, the Vector rewriting his momentum from forward to lateral and carrying him through an arc that ended against the Fold’s wall, and then Noah pulled again before Ragnar had processed the wall contact, and Ragnar swung the other direction, and Noah hit him twice more during the swing as he swung this man like a rag doll while waving his hands like a conductor!
The cracks in Ragnar’s chest were no longer localized.
"Haha." The laugh came out shorter than usual, the sound of a being genuinely impressed through the pain. "You can...you can actually move me now. When did that-"
Noah waved him in a full rotation.
Ragnar went around the space like something being swung rather than something moving, and at the end of the rotation Noah let him find the wall again!
BOOM!
The Fold shuddered.
The flames around Noah were dense enough now to make his form difficult to resolve clearly, the multicolored obsidian fire churning in slow massive waves, and inside them the heartbeat started!
BOOM. BOOM. BOOM.

Pure Pressure. Each beat of it pushing outward from Noah’s position and meeting the Fold’s walls and returning, the rhythm of Persevere stacking building a cadence that the space around him was now physically expressing. Every second. Every utterance!
Ragnar was back on his feet and still grinning.
"I hate to admit this."He looked at his hands, at the Prime Cause expressions burning through them, and then at the churning wall of fire that was Noah. "But this...this is actually something."
Noah moved his tail and his arms together as he felt like it was time.

Slowly. Deliberately. The tail coming forward from behind, the clawed arms coming in from either side, all three converging toward a single point in front of his chest and pressing together until the combined shape formed a spear. His own body. His Primus Apeiron form becoming the weapon rather than wielding one.
He reached for Ragnar with THE Infinite Vector.
Not Ragnar’s momentum this time.
All of Ragnar. Every directional commitment his Silurian Paleozoic foundations were currently making. Noah rewrote all of it to one direction.
Toward him.
Ragnar felt it as his eyes went wide for the first time in the battle, and then the Vector’s full force brought him forward, and Noah held the spear-point of his body still, and Ragnar arrived!
BOOM!
The sound was that of something being split.

Ragnar V49 came apart at the center, the spear-point of Noah’s form driving through the Prime Cause-hardened architecture of a Silurian Paleozoic Ira Gilded One with the force of accumulated Persevere elevations behind it, and the two halves came to rest on the floor of the Fold in the positions the momentum carried them to after the contact concluded.
Noah stood in the continuous multicolored obsidian flames, the heartbeat pressure still beating outward from him, his form still resolving slowly through the dense churning fire.
He looked at what remained of Ragnar V49.
The brutal smile was still on the torn face.
"Burr..ddy bb-ooy..." The voice came out smaller than it had been. The cognizance was still present, just inhabiting a significantly reduced operational context.
Noah crouched beside the closest half.
He started with what was in front of him.
Ragnar V49’s Source hit his jaws thst felt like a furnace of existence and the furnace processed it!
The laugh came through even then, genuine to the end!
The flames kept rising.
One per second!
Noah devoured Ragnar V49 the Fold filled with the sound of a heartbeat as an enemy that had pummeled him not too long ago...was dead!
Silurian Paleozoic Scale...he could now take down!

chapters.title: Chapter 5262: Quintessential Immensity! II
paragraphs: Defeating a Silurian Paleozoic Ragnar changed things in the way that a door opening changed things. On the other side of it was every other Ragnar in Observable Existence, V55 and V69 and V112 and the rest of them, each one Silurian Paleozoic with Prime Cause integrations and mass-produced architecture and the brutal competence of an entity designed from the beginning to be hard to kill. He could kill them now. He would kill them systematically, consuming each one, adding their Silurian Paleozoic foundations and their Prime Cause residues to everything he was building.
The hunt would continue.

His Infinite Scales had been sitting in a state he privately described as productive flux. Infinitas Architectura... the second demarcation, the construction of THE Hadean Pillar of Infinity and a lot more, had been running alongside Infinitas Causa, the integration of Causes into his existence, and the two tracks had been influencing each other. The Source. THE Primordial Tongue. THE Galdr Source developing in THE Source Lands. All of it was finding positions within the first Infinite Scale that the Scale’s original architecture hadn’t designated for them.
This was fine. The Scales were his. They moved when he moved!

The complication was scalability. The more he compressed into his first Infinite Scale of Existence, the harder it became to produce a version applicable to his followers. He could always strip it down, build a derivative framework that removed the components specific to what he alone was. But nothing regarding what he held could be considered normal, and the derivative would reflect that through how much stripping it required.
He’d address it when the gap demanded addressing.

His Primus Apeiron body was already moving through Observable Existence with the focused intent of a hunt that had finally found its appropriate tier, the Persevere flames burning in continuous one-second stacks as it pursued the scattered Ragnar clones across Transcendent Folds and Dead Wheels of Existence. That body had work to do and was doing it.
A different body appeared in the depths of THE Infiniverse!

The core of THE Infiniverse was not a place in the geographic sense. It was a condition... the point where the domain’s accumulated substance converged most completely, where the influence of the Primordial Realms and the Miniature Infinite Causes and the Calabi-Yau folding all pressed toward a single expression of what THE Infiniverse was becoming.

Boundless rivers of multicolored Infinity moved through it in every direction, the endless seas of the substance rising and falling around the currents in the rhythm of something alive that was learning to breathe.
THE Infiniverse stood at the center of it.
Her manifestation had changed since the last time he’d been here in person.

The bejeweled multicolored dress she wore now carried obsidian bands woven through its fabric, the terminal Infinity he’d been working with in THE Source Lands having found its way into her expression, the domain reflecting what he’d been doing the way domains reflected their architects.
Her eyes were bright on him the moment he appeared, the brightness of knowing already what he’d come to try.
She always knew.
He held out his hand.
She took it.
He paused the Persevere utterances. The continuous flames settling to their most recent elevated baseline, the compound stacks holding in place rather than climbing further.

"I share an unbreakable and quintessential connection with THE Infiniverse."He looked at her directly. "My Infinity flows alongside it. My Source is shared alongside it."He tightened his grip on her hand slightly. "The usage of Persevere shall be shared and applicable to it as well."
He held her gaze.

"The cost to do so will be unfathomably high. Utilizing a letter of THE Primordial Tongue on a single existence is already demanding enough. Utilizing it on a construct that spans countless domains, a structure with enough foundation to become an Observable Existence, the cost for even one utterance at that scale may be impossible to calculate."
He paused.
"But this cost shall be paid."He let it settle. "With Infinity."
BOOM.
The smile came before the silence was finished.
It started at the corners of his mouth and spread outward with the slow unstoppable motion of something that had decided on its full extent and was going to reach it regardless. It was too wide!
The teeth showing too many and too jagged, the grin stretching past what faces were designed to contain, his eyes narrowing into glowing manic slits of pure quintessential light!
THE Infiniverse matched him.

Her smile spread the same way, reached the same extreme, the same impossible width and the same sharp jagged fullness, her eyes going to the same narrow blazing slits, the manifestation of a domain that had spent its existence dreaming of this moment and had decided the moment had arrived!
Existence shuddered around both of them as they smiled devilishly!

Not the Fold, not the Infiniverse’s internal structure... existence itself, the surrounding arrangement of what was and what was becoming, registering two beings with identical deranged devilish smiles contemplating something that should not be attempted and showing every indication of attempting it anyway!
Noah looked at THE Infiniverse with the devilish glint that hadn’t left his narrowed eyes.
"Persevere."
HUUM.
The flames came.

They covered him first, the multicolored obsidian fire rising in the familiar waves but at a scale that matched the intention behind the utterance rather than the scale of a single existence... and then they spread onto THE Infiniverse’s manifestation, the fire covering her figure and her outstretched hands and the light in her eyes, and then they spread further, past her, onto the boundless multicolored seas of Infinity surrounding them, and then further still.
The three thousand realms took the flames.
The Primordial Realms... all of them took the flames of a single Primordial Tongue letter being applied at a scale the letter had never been applied at before.
Noah laughed.
It came out madly and he let it.
"The cost is Infinity." He said it to the roaring flames and the shuddering domain and THE Infiniverse’s matching expression. "Take as much as you want. Take all you want!"

He raised his free hand toward the burning seas. "Because from now on, every second I will Persevere alongside my Infiniverse. And I will pay this cost gladly... from now on, into whatever future holds."
BOOM!

The vast endless regions of countless gigaparsecs of domains already influenced by multiple causes burned with resplendence, the elevation of Persevere reaching every corner of THE Infiniverse’s accumulated expanse simultaneously, the compound reinforcement of the letter doing to the domain what it did to a single existence but across a structure that had never experienced it.
A second passed.
BOOM!
The flames built again.

Every component of THE Infiniverse, every realm, every cause, every developing Primordial space, every sea of accumulated Infinity... received the second utterance’s elevation stacked on the first’s baseline.
Oh!

|The sustained application of Persevere has accelerated the domain’s foundational development beyond projected timelines. The compound elevation of a Primordial Tongue letter applied continuously at domain scale is producing effects that no framework has been able to model.|
|THE Infiniverse has built sufficient foundation. The reinforcement, elevation, and enhancement of THE Primordial Tongue letter applied continuously has paved the way for the next stage.|
|THE Infinite Cause is ready for its emergence.|
|A moment of paramount quintessence is approaching.|
|THE Infiniverse shall Persevere.|

On the other side of it was every other Ragnar in Observable Existence, V55 and V69 and V112 and the rest of them, each one Silurian Paleozoic with Prime Cause integrations and mass-produced architecture and the brutal competence of an entity designed from the beginning to be hard to kill.
He could kill them now.
He would kill them systematically, consuming each one, adding their Silurian Paleozoic foundations and their Prime Cause residues to everything he was building.
The hunt would continue.
His Infinite Scales had been sitting in a state he privately described as productive flux.

Infinitas Architectura... the second demarcation, the construction of THE Hadean Pillar of Infinity and a lot more, had been running alongside Infinitas Causa, the integration of Causes into his existence, and the two tracks had been influencing each other.
The Source.
THE Primordial Tongue.
THE Galdr Source developing in THE Source Lands.
All of it was finding positions within the first Infinite Scale that the Scale’s original architecture hadn’t designated for them.
This was fine.
The Scales were his.
They moved when he moved!
The complication was scalability.
The more he compressed into his first Infinite Scale of Existence, the harder it became to produce a version applicable to his followers.
