chapters.title: Chapter 5263: Quintessential Immensity! III
paragraphs: The Early Veiled Shore burned beautifully.

Noah walked its golden sands with his hands behind his back and watched the multicolored flames of Persevere move through the Infinite Herbs growing in their fields along the waterline, each plant burning with the letter’s warmth and coming out of it more than it had been going in.

The golden sands themselves held the heat differently than they had before the utterance, the Infinity within each grain denser, the warmth of THE Source Lands’ Galdr development running through him and into the domain at the same one-second cadence.
THE Early Veiled Shore was his favorite part of THE Infiniverse.
He’d never said this to anyone. But it was true, and the truth of it was visible in how often he came here when one of his bodies needed to simply be somewhere for a moment rather than do something.
He kept walking.

Through the Three Thousand Realms, past the Primordial domains. The flames were everywhere, running through the domain’s full expanse at the one-second cadence of a letter being applied to something vast enough to take a full second to receive each application.
In one region.
THE Beholder and THE Mnemonic Leviathan floated near Amelia Osmont’s position. His mother was watching the flames move through the domain with bright eyes.
THE Beholder’s singular cognizance pressed against Noah’s awareness as he approached, the oldest warning it had given him surfacing.
It had warned him. The emergence of an Observable Existence drew catastrophe. The Gilded would find it. Things from beyond either of those categories may find it. It had told him to stop.
He’d told THE Beholder he couldn’t stop!

The logic was simple, even if the stakes weren’t. He had simple dreams...of peace, stability, and safety for himself and his people. Stopping and accepting the limitations imposed on him meant remaining at a level where something more powerful could come and take everything he’d built.

Today THE Infiniverse would become an Observable Existence, and whatever came after that could come. He’d built the Calabi-Yau foldings to hide her. He’d taken every available concealment measure. Now he simply had to watch the glory of it happen!
He looked at his mother and smiled as he walked on.
Elsewhere in Observable Existence, his Primus Apeiron form was moving.

Ragnar V55 was in the remnant of a Dead Wheel of Existence, the former Civilizational structure collapsed into fragments that drifted through the void in slow disconnected rotation. He was hunting the scattered Gilded Ones displaced by his Directives, and he had found one.
THE Primus Apeiron didn’t slow.

The continuous Persevere flames running through the Primus Apeiron form had been stacking for longer than the original battle with V49 had taken, the compound elevation pressing through the Apeiron scales in waves that the Dead Wheel’s fragments reflected back as multicolored light.

Noah drove his tail through the Wheel fragment Ragnar V55 was using as cover at a speed that made cover a concept rather than a protection, the spear-tip singularity arriving at V55’s position before V55 had finished registering the tail’s departure point.
He was not even able to say anything before dense Infinity and boundless Galdr Source pierced his existence!
V55 went down. Noah ate what remained and kept moving.

A Sororis Prima had taken shelter near THE Wyld’s outer borders, her Silurian Paleozoic Source expression pressed as small as she could manage in the hope that low profile would equal safety. THE Infinite Vector felt her power moving through the Fold’s architecture before she felt the Primus Apeiron entering it.
Noah appeared with brutal immensity and crushed her where she stood!
He ate what remained.

Three more Ragnars in a cluster had formed a defensive arrangement in one of the Dead Folds, their Prime Cause expressions covering the approach vectors with the coordinated efficiency of mass-produced entities running identical programming.

Noah came at the arrangement from above with an Infinity expression backed by all three of his active Causes simultaneously, the compound force of THE Bellum Cause, THE Cognitio Cause, and THE Infinite Cause hitting the defensive arrangement from outside the vectors it had been calibrated to cover as he landed like a beast and tore them apart, all the while belllowing to them...
"PERSEVERE!"
BOOM!
He ate what remained.
The Primus Apeiron form moved through Observable Existence with the calm thoroughness of a hunt that had found its appropriate scale!
<THE Braneworld Observable Existence>
In a Superbius citadel that stood countless Gigaparsecs from THE Velanthra in THE Braneworld Observable Existence, the towers were high and golden and designed to communicate pride.

The citadel rose from its base in tiered platforms, each tier gilded and broad, the towers themselves climbing from the upper platforms in spires that caught the ambient Observable Force of THE Braneworld and channeled it downward through the structure’s foundations like architecture that fed on its own environment.

From the outside it was magnificent. The gold of the Superbius House that owned it ran through every surface, the specific gold of sovereignty rather than decoration, and the millions of Gilded Ones that populated its lower tiers moved through it with ease.
At the highest tower’s highest room, Sororis Prima Elizabeth stepped out.
She was pulling on white-gold robes as she walked, fingers moving through the fastenings with the automatic efficiency of someone who’d dressed quickly in this sequence many times.
The room she’d left held bodies. Luxuria bodies, broken, naked, and collapsed of their existence. Her eyes held a brutal light as she finished the last fastening.
Her power registered at a level that made Silurian Paleozoic Scale feel like a waypoint rather than a destination. Beyond Devonian even.

At the transition between THE Third Scale and THE Fourth, or fully within THE Fourth...the distinction was difficult to establish from outside her foundations, her expression too contained to broadcast the finer details.
She stretched. She yawned.
She took out a golden medallion.
"Nothing has been heard from those sent to the lower Observable Existence to oversee the newly appearing anomaly."Her voice was sharp and flat.

"With the emergence of a Relictus still being hunted from there, and this current situation, the appearing anomaly can be labeled a Relictus as well. The lower Observable Existence has become a breeding ground." She paused. "THE Magna Sorora has given permission for a Gilded Legion to be deployed. I will personally lead it. Get the Ira and other components ready."
A crisp reply came through the medallion.
"Understood."
She cracked her neck.
She still didn’t feel satisfied.

The broken Luxuria in the room behind her hadn’t been enough. It never was... or rather, it was, but the window between enough and not-enough had been narrowing across the centuries, and she’d never bothered to examine why.
What held interest was the activity. The specific sensation of power applied directly to a lesser existence until the existence gave way.
Nothing replicated it. Not cultivation breakthroughs. Not victories. Not the administrative satisfaction of a well-executed Legion.
She looked toward the golden door at the far end of the corridor.
"Bring in the other Luxuria tools."

The door opened. Ten of them entered, their heads down, their expressions dim with the accumulated weight of what this tower required of them. She watched them enter with the evaluating attention she brought to everything.
She waved her hand.
The one at the front was pulled forward by the force of it, their body crossing the room without their feet generating the movement, and her arms came around their neck.
She felt the pressure build as she crushed his neck, feeling his existence folding and collapsing as she applied the very force of her causes into her grip.
She felt the giving until his existence...collapsed in her hands, her eyes burning with the thrill!

Hundreds of thousands had given beneath her hands over the course of her existence. She remembered none of their faces. She remembered none of their names. She remembered only the sensation, which was the only part that had ever mattered to her.
The Legion would be ready soon.
She could wait!

chapters.title: Chapter 5264: The Gilded Legion
paragraphs: Berserker Mbaku had stood in front of many legions over his life.
This one felt...grand!

He stood at the forward edge of the golden clearing and looked back across it. One hundred Silurian Ragnars occupied the left flank, their formations tight and identical, each face wearing the same brutal expression on the same face, the mass-produced perfection of them both impressive and faintly unsettling even to someone who’d worked alongside them before.

The nine hundred Silurian Ira Gilded Ones behind them moved with the disciplined restlessness of warriors who had been told to wait and were tolerating it. Five hundred Silurian Superbius Gilded Ones held the center, their bearing erect, their Existential Radiation pressing outward through the golden air of the clearing.
The ten Devonian Ragnars stood apart from their Silurian counterparts in the way that things operating at a different tier always stood apart. His own Devonian standing recognized theirs.

The ten Sororis Primas were distributed through the formation. Each carried the Devonian authority alongside their Custodes that made them the backbone of what this Legion was rather than ornament added to it.

Above the clearing, ten massive oval vessels floated in the arrangement the Avaritia engineering houses had long ago determined was optimal. The Avaritia had designed them, as they designed everything the other designations relied on without acknowledging the reliance. The vessels were golden, flattened at their bases and curved through their upper architecture into the oval shape that provided maximum internal volume for the Legion’s components. Their surfaces caught the ambient light of THE Braneworld and held it, the gold warm rather than blinding.

Mbaku rolled his shoulders. His half-bull frame settled into its combat posture without requiring instruction, it had been doing that for eons, the body making the preparation while the mind handled the assessment. Three Prime Cause integrations burned in his foundations with the quiet readiness of capabilities that had been integrated long enough to feel like physiology rather than technique.
He was sweeping the formation when something snagged his attention and held it.

Behind the third Sororis Prima from the left. A group that hadn’t been in any briefing he’d received, positioned just far enough inside the Legion’s formation to belong to it and just conspicuously enough assembled to not quite blend into it.
He looked at them.

A young man with purple-gold hair stood toward the front, his fair skin covered in archaic crimson tattoos that shifted position while Mbaku watched. His pupils were gold and blue at once, burning simultaneously, and a loose crown of Observable Force orbited his head without resting on it. He was looking at everything in the clearing with the careful attention of someone assembling a thorough picture of a situation they had not expected to find themselves in.

Beside him, a woman with crimson hair that moved without any wind present and eyes that held the brightness of someone who already knew how things were going to go. She emanated nothing. No power signature, no Cause expression, no ambient pressure of any kind.

The one-eyed man behind her had obsidian skin over a frame that communicated nothing decorative, and there was a woman with fiery green hair and a green dress emanated verdant holy light in slow waves that felt nurturing and wrong simultaneously, her face covered by a blindfold.
A slime, and a man with rivers of golden Infinity orbiting him.

Lastly, a petite woman’s eyes moved across every surface in the clearing in rapid calculating passes, the intelligence behind them her most dominant feature. She held the tension of someone whose instincts had been right enough times that ignoring them was no longer something she considered. She was...the one who looked the oddest to him as Mbaku could almost say she was a Bounded Lifeform.
Since when did Bounded Lifeforms begin walking freely in THE Braneworld Observable Existence?
Mbaku looked at this group for a long moment as it truly felt out of place

Most of them he couldnt feel the auras of, which meant they were either Devonian...or had stepped onto THE Fourth Scale of Existence. Which was not realisitic for them to be behind the scenes and not leading this Legion.
Then he shook his head.

He didn’t question the Sororis Prima they stood behind. By extension, he didn’t question THE Magna Sorora, which meant he didn’t question the presence of beings in this formation that he couldn’t immediately classify.
He had served long enough to know that the things he couldn’t classify were frequently the Magna Sorora’s business and only incidentally his.
He looked forward.
HUUM!
Sororis Prima Elizabeth descended from the upper air of the clearing and the formation held its posture with the automatic discipline of a Legion in the presence of its commander.
She was unhurried. She looked across the assembled force with eyes that caught the ambient gold of the vessels above and returned it colder.
"Stand ready and proud."Her voice reached the formation’s full extent without being raised. "Stand ready... for we do not make mistakes."
The golden vessels above began buzzing.
A Legion had formed, ready to descend into the lower Observable Existence.

What most of them hadn’t registered... what Mbaku had noticed and filed without questioning and what the broader formation had not noticed at all...was the group standing behind one of the ten Sororis Primas.
They were odd, those beings. They were odd in ways that didn’t resolve cleanly into any category the Gilded framework provided.
Very few beings, if any, in THE Braneworld knew the truth of it: that almost all of these odd unknown beings who were now part of this Gilded Legion...didn’t belong in this time and era.
Several didn’t belong in this Observable Existence at all.
Among them, two were particularly worth noting.
The woman with the rapid calculating eyes was watching everything with suspicion.

And the young man with the purple-gold hair and the shifting tattoos and the crown of orbiting Observable Force was watching everything carefully, composedly, with the attention of someone who had come here with intentions he was not broadcasting.
His name...was Achilles Adrastia!

A young man with purple-gold hair stood toward the front, his fair skin covered in archaic crimson tattoos that shifted position while Mbaku watched.
His pupils were gold and blue at once, burning simultaneously, and a loose crown of Observable Force orbited his head without resting on it.
He was looking at everything in the clearing with the careful attention of someone assembling a thorough picture of a situation they had not expected to find themselves in.
Beside him, a woman with crimson hair that moved without any wind present and eyes that held the brightness of someone who already knew how things were going to go.
She emanated nothing.
No power signature, no Cause expression, no ambient pressure of any kind.

The one-eyed man behind her had obsidian skin over a frame that communicated nothing decorative, and there was a woman with fiery green hair and a green dress emanated verdant holy light in slow waves that felt nurturing and wrong simultaneously, her face covered by a blindfold.
A slime, and a man with rivers of golden Infinity orbiting him.
Lastly, a petite woman’s eyes moved across every surface in the clearing in rapid calculating passes, the intelligence behind them her most dominant feature.
She held the tension of someone whose instincts had been right enough times that ignoring them was no longer something she considered.
She was...the one who looked the oddest to him as Mbaku could almost say she was a Bounded Lifeform.
Since when did Bounded Lifeforms begin walking freely in THE Braneworld Observable Existence?
Mbaku looked at this group for a long moment as it truly felt out of place
Most of them he couldnt feel the auras of, which meant they were either Devonian...or had stepped onto THE Fourth Scale of Existence.
Which was not realisitic for them to be behind the scenes and not leading this Legion.
Then he shook his head.
He didn’t question the Sororis Prima they stood behind.
By extension, he didn’t question THE Magna Sorora, which meant he didn’t question the presence of beings in this formation that he couldn’t immediately classify.
He had served long enough to know that the things he couldn’t classify were frequently the Magna Sorora’s business and only incidentally his.
He looked forward.
HUUM!
Sororis Prima Elizabeth descended from the upper air of the clearing and the formation held its posture with the automatic discipline of a Legion in the presence of its commander.
She was unhurried.
She looked across the assembled force with eyes that caught the ambient gold of the vessels above and returned it colder.
"Stand ready and proud."Her voice reached the formation’s full extent without being raised.
"Stand ready... for we do not make mistakes."
The golden vessels above began buzzing.
A Legion had formed, ready to descend into the lower Observable Existence.

What most of them hadn’t registered... what Mbaku had noticed and filed without questioning and what the broader formation had not noticed at all...was the group standing behind one of the ten Sororis Primas.
They were odd, those beings.
They were odd in ways that didn’t resolve cleanly into any category the Gilded framework provided.
Very few beings, if any, in THE Braneworld knew the truth of it: that almost all of these odd unknown beings who were now part of this Gilded Legion...didn’t belong in this time and era.
Several didn’t belong in this Observable Existence at all.
Among them, two were particularly worth noting.
The woman with the rapid calculating eyes was watching everything with suspicion.

And the young man with the purple-gold hair and the shifting tattoos and the crown of orbiting Observable Force was watching everything carefully, composedly, with the attention of someone who had come here with intentions he was not broadcasting.
His name...was Achilles Adrastia!

chapters.title: Chapter 5265: Across Time and Existence! I
paragraphs: Heralictus said war was the father of all things and king of all.

He wrote this in a treatise that would survive longer than every building he’d ever entered, arguing with the calm assurance of someone who believed they had located the first principle beneath everything else!

Peace was not a condition. Peace was the absence of conflict between conflicts, the brief intermission where opposing forces caught their breath before resuming the violence that actually drove existence forward.
Harmony was stagnation, and stagnation led to decay, and decay led to the collapse of whatever complacent arrangement had mistaken its temporary equilibrium for a permanent state.

Change required destruction. Progress required brutal opposition. The only existences that grew were the ones that fought, and the only civilizations that endured were the ones that understood fighting as foundational rather than aberrant.
Adversity was good. War was good!

This was what Heralictus believed completely and wrote about extensively and defended against every colleague who challenged the thesis across the full span of his scholarly career.In his entire life, he never once touched mana.He never cultivated a single day. He lived and died on the floor of existence he’d been born on and experienced none of the wars his work insisted were necessary for the progression of all things.
The thesis was correct.
He had simply never been in a position to verify it personally!
The last three Ragnars had gone down within minutes of each other.

V287 first. He’d been sheltering inside the remains of a shattered Shelter of THE Loom. It hadn’t mattered. The other two fell after a few exchanges as he...had gotten very good at taking down Silurian Paleozoic Scale Gilded Ones!
He ate all three.

The Primus Apeiron form processed. Each Ragnar was a Silurian Paleozoic existence with two integrated Prime Causes and mass-produced Ira engineering, and each one’s consumption added measurable density to what he was carrying as the loot from them...was even enough to act as fuel to unlock more of his Ego designations.He absolutely had enough to unlock multiple Sins and Virtues as soon as things died down.
He sat in the wreckage of the Shelter and thought.
He was thriving.

Not in the general sense that he was winning, though he was winning. In the sense that his existence was doing what it was built to do at a pace it was built to sustain, and the results were confirming every structural decision he’d made across the climb.

THE Primordial Tongue’s first letter was his. The loophole that made the letter pull from Infinity instead of his Source was his. The continuous one-per-second Persevere stacking that made his Primus Apeiron form measurably stronger with each heartbeat was his. THE Infiniverse was undergoing her transformation into an Observable Existence at this very moment, the compound elevation of Persevere applied at domain scale doing in seconds what natural development would have taken eons to produce.
The joy of it was genuine!

He’d always liked doing impossible things. The word impossible carried a specific invitation for him that it didn’t carry for most beings. When someone said a thing couldn’t be done, what he heard was that nobody had tried it with his particular combination of resources and willingness, and the combination had not yet encountered its ceiling.

THE Cheating Architect and THE Protagonist sat in his Source as constituent components of what he was, and what they contributed wasn’t a technique or a capability but an orientation... his existence looked at closed systems and instinctively found the gap where the system’s designers hadn’t accounted for him.
The Primordial Tongue had a cost. His existence had found the gap. The gap was Infinity.
Part of him was the concept of cheating!

His good mood extended beyond his own advancement. He’d left Gilded Ones scattered through Observable Existence for those who needed them. Eckert had his targets. Alexander had his. Emotive was hunting with the terrifying combination of her Absolute Luxuria form and the Ira Gilded Ones she’d stripped of will and turned into a team.
THE Primordial Paradox was doing whatever THE Primordial Paradox , and Noah didn’t need to manage that because THE Primordial Paradox had been operating independently for too long.

His people in their Apeiron forms were building their adversity through the engagements he’d reserved for them, collapsing and returning and collapsing again and becoming stronger through the cycle the engineering was designed to produce.
Everything was moving!
THE Infiniverse was about to become an Observable Existence.
At the height of this, at the very peak of the good feeling... Noah’s eyes went sharp.
He’d been here before. He knew this part!

The pattern was reliable enough that he’d stopped treating it as coincidence and started treating it as a structural feature of his existence. Grand accomplishments arrived and settled into their proper positions and then, within a window so consistent it should have been assigned a formal designation,something inserted itself into the moment and refused to let the accomplishment breathe.
He looked around.

He looked left. Rivers of multicolored Infinity moved through the wreckage of the Shelter in their ordinary currents. He looked right. The multicolored seas of the surrounding space swished and settled without urgency. He looked up. He looked down. He extended his perception through the full mile of the Primus Apeiron form’s current range and found nothing approaching, nothing gathering, nothing building toward a disruption.
He waited.
Nothing.
He waited longer!
Still nothing!
The surrounding existence was calm. Aggressively calm. Calm enough that it felt less like nothing was coming and more like something was deliberately not coming yet.

He narrowed his eyes at the general direction of existence and stood his ground for a few more seconds, daring it. If something was going to happen, it could go ahead and happen while he was looking at it with his full attention.
Nothing happened.
Okay!
He started to turn away.
HUUM!
And right fucking then...

Something buzzed above. His Infinity burned bright and his Source compressed into combat readiness without him requesting it, his Primus Apeiron form orienting toward the upper space with the speed of a body that had been doing nothing but fight for the last several minutes and had not yet downshifted. His eyes tracked the disturbance with sharp focus.
Had the response from THE Braneworld come faster than the Directives’ information quarantine could hold?
He prepared for whatever was about to descend from the upper reaches of Observable Existence!
"AHH!"
It was not a Gilded One’s entry signature.

It was a scream. A very normal scream, from a very normal-sounding voice, and when Observable Force flickered and deposited the screaming thing into the air above the shattered Shelter, what he saw was a small woman falling toward him with her arms extended in directions that suggested the falling had not been planned.

She...was not a Gilded One. He confirmed this in the first instant of perceiving her. No engineered Ego. No Observable Force density that exceeded what a Bounded Lifeform carried. She was small and petite and falling, and when she hit the sea, she bounced!
She stood up fast.
"Sir Osmontian, don’t kill me! Hear me out first!"

chapters.title: Chapter 5266: Across Time and Existence! II
paragraphs: Her eyes were the only part of her face that couldn’t hold still.

They moved across everything, his Primus Apeiron form, the surrounding destruction, the consumed Ragnar remains, back to his form, in rapid calculating passes that held more processing speed than the rest of her presentation suggested.
"I come in peace! In peace, you hear?!" She had both hands up. "Even though I made a deal with Adrastia to keep me alive with his Persevere, I still don’t want to try fighting you!"
She closed her eyes.

She opened them slowly, looking at him from between half-closed lids as though she needed to confirm he hadn’t moved during the closing, and when she confirmed he hadn’t, something shifted in her face. The nervous energy remained, but underneath it a bright satisfaction appeared.
She put her fists on her waist.
She straightened up, took a breath, and looked at him with an expression that was attempting composure and achieving something adjacent to it.

"Ahem." She cleared her throat. "Sir Osmontian. Or is it THE Primus Apeiron? Whatever title you go by now." Her voice steadied. "I, Taylor of The Light, come in peace. I have actually come to strike a deal with you."
Noah looked at her.
She’d said these things in her opening sentence without any preamble.
Her eyes were still moving.
He focused his perception on her. THE Infinite Tongue extended toward whatever substrate composed her existence and looked for what it could pull.
Nothing.

He pushed Pillow Talk outward toward her. The capability that made existence itself confess its information to him, the passive flow that had been delivering names and standings and Cause integrations and hidden details of every being he’d encountered since activating it, reached for whatever Taylor of The Light was carrying beneath her unremarkable exterior.
Nothing came back.Just nothing. The space where information about her should have been was empty!
|Entity identification: Taylor of The Light.|
|Additional information: unavailable. Pillow Talk returns no data beyond the designation provided. THE Infinite Tongue finds no additional substrate.|

Noah looked at this woman and his tail moved behind him slow and deliberate, the spear-tip singularity at its end tracing a lazy arc through the air that didn’t hide what the lazy arc was designed for.
His deep voice came out through the Primus Apeiron form.
"What deal are you talking about?" The crystalline blue of his eyes held her without blinking. "There are more of you? You mentioned Persevere. Someone with access to THE Primordial Tongue?"
His tail completed its arc and began another. "Speak quickly. Make things clear."
Taylor of The Light looked at the tail.
She looked at it for a full second before she looked at his face, and then she looked at the tail again, and then she cleared her throat.
"Err, sir.Do you have a less scary and more friendly form? It’s fucking imposing trying to talk to you while you look like a beast who’s trying to kill me with your eyes and tail alone."
Noah smiled.

The smile was brutal and unhurried and showed too many teeth, and the tail behind him didn’t slow its arc, and the Persevere flames running through his Primus Apeiron form burned a fraction brighter as the smile formed.
"This is my most friendly form."
Taylor physically squirmed.
She took a breath. Steadied herself. Looked at a point approximately six inches to the left of his face, which was apparently easier to address than the face itself.

"Well." She sighed. "It’s a long story, but I’ll make it short. Basically, whatever you do in the future is so fucking batshit crazy that right now, there is an assassination team of beings from the future who came back to this time, where you are apparently just starting out, so they can fuck you up."
BOOM!
She said this casually!
Noah’s eyes flashed. An assassination team!

From the future. Sent backward through time to this moment, specifically this moment, when he was in the early stages of what his existence was becoming, to eliminate him before what he was becoming arrived at its full expression.

He’d wanted time to absorb his gains. He’d wanted days. He’d wanted to stack Persevere and let the compound elevation do what compound elevation did when given time to accumulate without interruption. He’d wanted THE Infiniverse to complete her transformation and his Infinite Scales to solidify around the new components he’d been adding!
And here was something. Because there was always something.
From the future. Fucking something from the future!
Taylor was still talking.
"Frankly, I don’t think it’s fair." She had her arms crossed now and was addressing the general direction of the sky with the energy of someone filing a formal complaint.

"They are sore losers who can’t kill you in the future, so they come back and try and kill you now? Fucking scrubs, man. If you and I were fighting or we were mortal enemies, I would scheme to kill you straight on."She pointed at him. "Oh, but again, I am not your enemy. Or really, I don’t want to be. If only these fuckers knew what existence was saying about you-"
"Focus for me," Noah said. "Continue. Concisely without rambling."
She stopped mid-sentence.

She blinked. Cleared her throat. Looked around as though what she was about to say required checking whether anyone else was listening, which was absurd given that they were in the wreckage of a shattered Shelter of THE Loom surrounded by consumed Ragnar remains and nothing else.
She floated closer to him.

All the fear she’d shown upon arrival was apparently gone, replaced by the conspiratorial energy of someone who’d decided that if she was going to be in proximity to something terrifying, she might as well commit to the proximity fully. She looked left. Looked right. Leaned in until she was approximately three feet from his Primus Apeiron face.
She whispered.
"These fuckers from the future. They came and kidnapped me and a few other anomalies from different Observable Existences."
Her whisper... was louder than most people’s normal speaking voice.

"Beings with unique capabilities who could counter you momentarily while they do their thing. They fucking kidnapped me in the middle of my centennial family gathering."She pulled back slightly. "I had my whole Observable Existence there. Oh, which I rule, by the way?"
She paused.
"Isn’t that fucking cool? I, a Bounded Lifeform, rule the entire lower Observable Existence where I come from."She put her hand on her chest. "It’s actually a matter of pride. Huhu!"
"Focus."

"Ahem. Right. They ruined my celebration, kidnapped me, threatened my people, and brought me to THE Braneworld Observable Existence. That’s where they’re coming from now. A Gilded Legion is being assembled as we speak."Her eyes moved in rapid passes across the wreckage around them.

"There are other anomalies up there. One guy who seems really good at controlling Infinity. His control even exceeds some Gilded Ones. But I’ve already compared what I can pull about him against what existence has told me about you." She shook her head. "He’s in for a fucking surprise."
She counted on her fingers.
"There are others meant to counter you. One that might have given you actual trouble is the one I mentioned. Achilles Adrastia." Her voice dropped into something more measured.

"His information is unique. He can apparently assimilate anything. But he’s also smart enough to not want any part of this assassination, so him and I formed a deal. He protects me from something like you, since existence told me he had a connection to THE Primordial Tongue, and I was confident enough to come here first."
She tapped something small and bright in her palm. "He gave me this little singularity so he might actually be listening."
She held up the singularity.
"Hey, Adrastia, can you hear me? Things aren’t going to absolute shit so far!" She waited. Nothing. "Hey, can you hear me?"She looked at the singularity. "Maybe he’s shy."

He protects me from something like you, since existence told me he had a connection to THE Primordial Tongue, and I was confident enough to come here first."
She tapped something small and bright in her palm.
"He gave me this little singularity so he might actually be listening."
She held up the singularity.
"Hey, Adrastia, can you hear me?
Things aren’t going to absolute shit so far!" She waited.
Nothing.
"Hey, can you hear me?"She looked at the singularity.
"Maybe he’s shy."

chapters.title: Chapter 5267: Across Time and Existence! III
paragraphs: Noah took all of it in.
He processed the information in layers!

First layer: beings from the future. This was the most significant piece because it implied his existence’s trajectory produced consequences severe enough that entities in that future considered temporal travel a proportionate response.

Second... they’d kidnapped anomalies from other Observable Existences to build a fucking existential squad. Specialized tools for a specialized target. Third...at least two of their tools, Taylor and this Adrastia, had independently decided they didn’t want to participate and were approaching him with defection as their opening offer.
He looked at Taylor.

She was a ruler of an Observable Existence. A Bounded Lifeform who’d done what he was doing from a different direction, climbing past the limitations imposed by her starting classification and arriving at a position that shouldn’t have been available to her. This alone made her more interesting than many.

Beings who ruled Observable Existences without Gilded engineering behind them didn’t exist by accident. She had the ability to back it up, and the fact that Pillow Talk couldn’t pull anything from her suggested the capability had substance behind it.
"So what’s the deal you want?" he said. "And your anomalous factor. What is it exactly?"
Taylor smiled and straightened up.

"Simple. Adrastia and I don’t want fuck all to do with this, and we would like that known. Our safety and eventual return to our respective Observable Existences would be ideal. Without these time-traveling fuckers getting vindictive and killing our families."She held up a finger. "As for my ability..."
The smile turned into something that was pride underneath the casual exterior.

"I am so fucking astonishing that Infinity and THE Primordial Source all talk to me. I don’t have access to the letters of THE Primordial Tongue or THE Source itself, and I dabble a little in Infinity, but I talk, and existence loves to talk back. They kidnapped me for this. To make sure they could track and kill all your bodies, wherever they are."
Her eyes moved in their rapid calculating passes.

"Existence told me that somehow, you have another body up there in THE Braneworld Observable Existence?" She tilted her head."I didn’t believe that at first. With how powerful THE Gilded Ones are, they wouldn’t leave a beast like you roaming around freely up there, right?"
She paused.

"As for down here, I can pull information about many parts of you. Most of you is clustered in a place filled with paradoxes where I can get very little info. What is that, what is it called..."She squinted. "THE Infiniverse? I was barely able to pull that name. What is-"
HUUM!

The pressure around Noah’s form changed. He didn’t do it deliberately. His Infinity and his Source responded to the name being spoken by an outside entity, and what they produced was a shift in the ambient weight of the space that made the multicolored seas around them go still.
Taylor felt the change.

She blinked. Her body drifted backward without her feet moving, a slow float away from his head that she wasn’t generating consciously. Her eyes stopped their calculating movement and held very still on his face.

"Woah." She raised both hands."I didn’t mean anything by that, big guy. I have, um, been told that I can talk too much. If I am, just stop me. I had a Relictus just leave halfway through my talking without me even realizing it, so I understand!" Her hands stayed up. "But remember. I come in peace!"
"So." She lowered her hands one at a time. "What are we doing here, monster friend? Beast friend? Anomaly friend?"

She tried each one and discarded each one. "You know what, I’ll stick to Osmontian. What shall we do about the squad of assassins trying to fuck you up, and how can we extricate me and Adrastia from this? I’d rather be back home right now not dealing with any of this shit."
Noah’s eyes flashed.
What to do.

He knew what he wanted to do. He loved adversity. He’d built an entire engineering framework around the principle that adversity was the mechanism of progression, and he’d been living that principle across every battle since his arrival in THE Braneworld. He’d sought it out. He’d initiated it!
He’d declared war on Gilded Ones specifically to produce the challenge and risk his advancement required.
And right now, he wanted a break from it.

Not because he was tired. Not because the adversity had exceeded his capacity. Because he’d just gained Persevere at zero cost and the compound elevation was stacking every second, and what that meant was that every second of peace was a second of growth that didn’t require a fight to produce!
The Primordial Tongue letter was doing the work. He didn’t need to supplement it with combat adversity right now. He needed time.
A few days. Just a few days of the Persevere stacking without interruption!
Or a few months. If he did something he’d never done before and simply let time pass. Observable Existence wouldn’t end in a few months, right?
Wars would still be there when he returned to them. Adversity was a permanent condition. It didn’t spoil. It didn’t expire. It waited!

And if he took that time. If he stacked Persevere every second for months. If THE Infiniverse completed her transformation and THE Infinite Cause reached its full emergence. If his Galdr Source continued its development in THE Source Lands alongside all of it.
By the time he came back to war...
"Hmm."
The smile started small.
It spread. It kept spreading, past the point where smiles normally stopped, the Primus Apeiron’s features pulling into something that carried delight and menace in equal measure.
His eyes narrowed into bright slits of crystalline blue above the widening grin, and the multicolored flames burning through his form responded to whatever he was thinking by burning hotter.
The surrounding existence trembled.
Taylor shivered!
She floated another foot backward. Her eyes, which had been moving constantly since her arrival, went very still.
"Bro." She looked at the trembling space around them. "This is why I wanted nothing to do with you. Because why the fuck is existence trembling now?"
She looked at him and then at the space and then at him again. "Hey, what did you just think to make the surrounding existence tremble? Fuck!"

chapters.title: Chapter 5268: Everybody Dies!
paragraphs: Noah looked at Taylor and thought about what she’d told him and found that not all of it fit.

Some of it did. An assassination team sent from the future was dramatic but not conceptually complicated, beings with enough power and enough motivation and enough temporal capability to execute a retroactive kill had existed.
But the logic anf specifics had problems.

"There’s a lot of possible things that can be done about this,"he said. His Primus Apeiron form looked at Taylor with the calm calculation of something that had been chewing on a thought and had reached the point where the thought was ready to be shared.
"But not all of it makes sense."
He let the Persevere flames settle slightly around his form.
"Coming through time is fine. I’ve traversed through time too. But...." He looked at the space around them.

"If they were really going to kill me, my future self would have already intervened. Existence is a closed loop. What was supposed to happen has happened and will happen. The past doesn’t change. What occurred in the past was already set, even if someone in the future thinks they’re going back to alter something. Whatever future they’re in won’t really change."He held her gaze.
"The past is set. If they come from the future, and I am alive in that future, then it means I never died."
WAA!

He straightened to his full height. The multicolored flames of Persevere burned across his Primus Apeiron form with the dense slow-churning warmth of continuous compound elevation, the surrounding seas of Infinity reflecting the multicolored light across the wreckage of the shattered Shelter.
"So all of this...is pointless."
BOOM!
Taylor looked at him.
Her rapid-moving eyes held still for approximately two seconds. She opened her mouth. Closed it. Opened it again.
"While your outlook on time seems right..."She paused. "Wowee, you are really full of yourself."
She caught herself. "Err, I mean, yes sir! You are invincible!"
His tail flickered.
She started to pull back, the beginnings of the cowering reflex she’d shown on arrival returning. But something behind her eyes caught and held, and the cowering didn’t complete.
She stood her ground, and the rapid movement of her eyes went still again, and what was behind them wasn’t nervous anymore.
"Hmm. Actually, no, fuck it." She looked at him directly.

"You are not invincible. I’ve seen multiple friends who believed they were invincible die. You too can die, no matter how terrifying you think you are. Even if you say the past can’t change and it’s already set and all that temporal bullshit."
Her voice dropped.
"Even you, Sir Osmontian, can die. Others more powerful than you have died."
The rapid movement came back into her eyes, but it was different now. The movement of someone looking at something far away.
"I have heard their deaths. I have heard Infinity and THE Primordial Source cry out for lifeforms born of Infinity and THE Primordial Source you can’t even imagine."
Lifeforms...born of Infinity and THE Primordial Source?
The air between them was quiet.
She flinched.

Her eyes shut and her shoulders came up and her body pulled back into the reflexive brace of someone who’d said something they believed and was now expecting the physical consequences of having said it. She held the brace for several seconds.
She opened one eye.
Then the other.
Noah hadn’t moved. His expression hadn’t changed. The flames burned. The tail had gone still.
She breathed out.
"Well. That’s just my experience and what I know." She straightened slowly. "But okay. The past is set. So what?"
Noah looked at her and felt something he hadn’t felt in a considerable time, which was the refreshment of a being who talked back. When was the last time someone had talked to him like that?
He shook his head and continued.

"Another thing,"he said. "If they came back in time, why not alert the strongest Fourth Scale Gilded Ones here? Or Fifth Scale, if that power exists?"He looked at the Shelter wreckage around them. "They could kill me easily at those tiers. But they haven’t. There should be a reason they can’t, which contributes to the closed loop theory."
Taylor blinked.

Her eyes lit up. She floated toward him again, the fear of thirty seconds ago apparently fully processed and discarded, her face carrying the brightness of someone who’d heard a question she had information about.

"Hey hey hey!"She was close to his head again. "So actually, I heard this woman Vireth, one of the time assassins, talking to a Sororis Prima in our party. She was saying how they’re hiding from existence. If they do anything too extreme, they’ll be noticed."
Her hands moved as she talked, the gestures carrying a rhythm that matched her speaking cadence.

"That’s why they recruited anomalies. Because if they involve Ealdor Gilded Ones, they’ll be detected. She said they have to walk a fine line. Them being here is already bad because they have to make sure THE Primordial Source doesn’t recognize them, since existence would reject them outright. They aren’t from here."
She leaned closer.

"Since I found that out, I’ve been screaming in my head that they don’t belong here. Whispering it. Shouting it. Trying to send this information through my communication with Infinity and THE Primordial Source."She dropped her hands.
"Fucking nothing happened. So if you have a direct line to the Source, that might be the easiest way to deal with them. Because why face a bunch of Fourth Scale fuckers if you don’t have to?"
Fourth Scale fuckers.

This was what wanted to interrupt the momentous occasion of THE Infiniverse becoming an Observable Existence. He’d just become capable of killing Silurian Paleozoic Scale entities, the middle tier of THE Third Scale!
The gap between that and Fourth Scale was not a gap he could currently close quickly.
But if he had time to continue allowing the spam of Persevere...
But for now, this Adversity didn’t need to happen.
A direct line to the Source. He didn’t have that. Not in the way Taylor was describing it, as a communication channel that could deliver a report and receive a response.
But he had a connection to something that did.
THE Creature.
THE Creature who held THE Primordial Source within his existence.

If Noah could get a message to him. If THE Creature’s connection to THE Primordial Source was direct enough to flag beings that didn’t belong in this time. If THE Primordial Source could be made aware, and if that awareness produced the rejection Taylor had described Vireth worrying about...
Then Noah wouldn’t need to fight Fourth Scale beings at all.
He’d just need to make a call.
"Hmmm."
The smile came back.

It spread across the Primus Apeiron form’s features with the slow devilish warmth. The multicolored flames of Persevere burned brighter around the smile, and the surrounding existence registered whatever he was thinking and held very still.
Taylor was watching.
Her eyes moved from his smile to the surrounding space and back to his smile.
"I... don’t like when you make that face,"she said!

chapters.title: Chapter 5269: THE Final Lesson!
paragraphs: <THE Creature>
THE Undefined Gaps had no patience for the weak.

It was a condition of the space itself, the dimensional territory between the classified arrangements of Observable Existence operating at a pressure that most beings processed as hostility and that THE Creature processed as background noise.
Around him, the battle was at full intensity.
The massive Relictus moved through the Gilded formations with the unhurried devastation of something that had been doing this for far too long.
The Devonian Paleozoic Scale Gilded Ones and THE Fourth Scale entities that had been sent against it were fully committed to an engagement that the Relictus was not.
It fought them the way terrain fought occupation... not by trying, but by being what it was.
THE Creature had his own work.

The Devonian Ragnars came at him in coordinated assault, three Causes burning through each one in compound expressions that turned the surrounding dimensional fabric of THE Undefined Gaps into a tactical mush they were trying to use against him.
THE Final Lesson met them.

His new stick, his goad was massive- obsidian, long, filled with the density of his Infinity and THE Primordial Source running through its length in twin currents that interacted where they met to produce something that was neither Infinity alone nor THE Primordial Source alone but both simultaneously.

He’d named it THE Final Lesson because everything he taught with it tended to be the last thing the recipient learned. He brought it around in a horizontal sweep that caught two Devonian Ragnars, the strike landing with the full weight of what THE Final Lesson carried, and the two Ragnars went sideways through THE Undefined Gaps’ dimensional fabric.
BOOM!
The third Ragnar drove in from behind.

THE Creature stepped aside. Brought THE Final Lesson straight down onto the Ragnar’s approach trajectory. The Ragnar hit it going forward and stopped going forward, and THE Creature pivoted without breaking rhythm and moved into the next one.
He was mid-swing when the message arrived.
It came through an Entanglement. The connection between him and THE Youngest that existed at a level beneath either of their power!
THE Youngest had used it directly. Infinity and THE Source both, as the transmission medium.
He paused long enough to absorb it.

"Hey. I wouldn’t normally reach out, but there is adversity being shoved down my throat I don’t particularly want right now. Here is information on some beings conducting actions they have to hide from THE Primordial Source. Are you able to pass on the message to whatever exists as a governing body or power from THE Primordial Source so they can take care of this?"
THE Creature’s expression shifted.

He smashed THE Final Lesson into the Devonian Ragnar directly in his path, the impact cracking through three of the Ragnar’s integrated Causes in a single contact, and sifted through the information Osmont had attached to the message.

Gilded Ones moving across time. A party operating from the future and concealing their temporal origin from THE Primordial Source because they knew what disclosure would produce. Actively working to alter a set past, which wasn’t temporal traversal in the closed-loop sense that he himself had performed here and there when the occasion required it.
He understood the distinction.

Closed-loop traversal left the past intact. Osmont had appeared in THE Earliest Folds and THE Infinite Unfurling because he had always appeared there. Every event had still occurred as it had occurred. THE Youngest had not changed anything. He had simply been the thing that was already there, the presence that had always been present, the closed loop confirming itself rather than disrupting itself.
What this party was doing was different.

They were actively seeking to alter outcomes. The past resisted this not through any sentimental attachment to how things had been but through structural necessity...existence derived its coherence from events having occurred as they occurred, and parties that tried to revise the set record introduced instabilities into that coherence that compounded outward.

THE Primordial Source did not tolerate instabilities. It didn’t tolerate them as a policy position. It was incapable of tolerating them the way a material was incapable of tolerating the conditions that caused it to fail.
Osmont had sent him accurate information.
THE Creature looked toward the Relictus.
He sent a short message.

One glance. The massive ancient being’s attention moved from the Fourth Scale Gilded One it had been occupying itself with and found THE Creature’s position. It held the look for a moment, the deep awareness behind its gaze taking in whatever THE Creature was communicating through the Entanglement they shared, and then it nodded once.
A single nod.
That was all.
THE Creature sent his reply back through the Entanglement toward THE Youngest, through Infinity and THE Source as the medium, the message traveling the same channel the question had traveled.
’THE Source will know. Existence will be rectified.’
BOOM!
He sent it and turned back to the engagement without further consideration.

The Devonian Ragnars had reorganized while he’d processed the exchange. They came in from three directions with their Cause expressions fully committed, the coordinated assault of beings who’d determined that individual approach hadn’t produced results and had decided collective approach was the next variable to test.
THE Final Lesson rose.

For beings like him, adversity was not something imposed. It wasn’t an interruption of something better. It was the closest thing he had to comfort, the constant companion that had never once left him across the full span of his existence, the only condition under which he felt his foundations operating at the level they were built to operate at.
He met the three Devonian Ragnars and the battle resumed.
Above him, the massive Relictus had already gone still.
Still in a way that was different from its combat stillness.

Still when one was communicating with something that didn’t require movement to receive the message. Its connection to THE Primordial Source ran deeper than any Gilded engineering had ever reached, deeper than any letter of THE Primordial Tongue could access, the direct channel of something that had been born from THE Source rather than something that had cultivated toward it.
THE Primordial Source was listening.

And existence, which had been carrying within it beings that didn’t belong in it, that were hiding from its governing awareness while they pursued revisions to outcomes it had already set, was about to become aware of what it was carrying.
THE Creature brought THE Final Lesson around and continued his work.
The rest would take care of itself.

THE Undefined Gaps had no patience for the weak.

It was a condition of the space itself, the dimensional territory between the classified arrangements of Observable Existence operating at a pressure that most beings processed as hostility and that THE Creature processed as background noise.
Around him, the battle was at full intensity.
The massive Relictus moved through the Gilded formations with the unhurried devastation of something that had been doing this for far too long.
The Devonian Paleozoic Scale Gilded Ones and THE Fourth Scale entities that had been sent against it were fully committed to an engagement that the Relictus was not.
It fought them the way terrain fought occupation... not by trying, but by being what it was.
THE Creature had his own work.

The Devonian Ragnars came at him in coordinated assault, three Causes burning through each one in compound expressions that turned the surrounding dimensional fabric of THE Undefined Gaps into a tactical mush they were trying to use against him.
THE Final Lesson met them.

His new stick, his goad was massive- obsidian, long, filled with the density of his Infinity and THE Primordial Source running through its length in twin currents that interacted where they met to produce something that was neither Infinity alone nor THE Primordial Source alone but both simultaneously.
He’d named it THE Final Lesson because everything he taught with it tended to be the last thing the recipient learned.

He brought it around in a horizontal sweep that caught two Devonian Ragnars, the strike landing with the full weight of what THE Final Lesson carried, and the two Ragnars went sideways through THE Undefined Gaps’ dimensional fabric.
BOOM!
The third Ragnar drove in from behind.
THE Creature stepped aside.
Brought THE Final Lesson straight down onto the Ragnar’s approach trajectory.
The Ragnar hit it going forward and stopped going forward, and THE Creature pivoted without breaking rhythm and moved into the next one.
He was mid-swing when the message arrived.
It came through an Entanglement.
The connection between him and THE Youngest that existed at a level beneath either of their power!
THE Youngest had used it directly.
Infinity and THE Source both, as the transmission medium.
He paused long enough to absorb it.
"Hey.
I wouldn’t normally reach out, but there is adversity being shoved down my throat I don’t particularly want right now.
Here is information on some beings conducting actions they have to hide from THE Primordial Source.
Are you able to pass on the message to whatever exists as a governing body or power from THE Primordial Source so they can take care of this?"
THE Creature’s expression shifted.

He smashed THE Final Lesson into the Devonian Ragnar directly in his path, the impact cracking through three of the Ragnar’s integrated Causes in a single contact, and sifted through the information Osmont had attached to the message.
Gilded Ones moving across time.
A party operating from the future and concealing their temporal origin from THE Primordial Source because they knew what disclosure would produce.
Actively working to alter a set past, which wasn’t temporal traversal in the closed-loop sense that he himself had performed here and there when the occasion required it.
He understood the distinction.
Closed-loop traversal left the past intact.
Osmont had appeared in THE Earliest Folds and THE Infinite Unfurling because he had always appeared there.
Every event had still occurred as it had occurred.
THE Youngest had not changed anything.
He had simply been the thing that was already there, the presence that had always been present, the closed loop confirming itself rather than disrupting itself.
What this party was doing was different.
They were actively seeking to alter outcomes.

The past resisted this not through any sentimental attachment to how things had been but through structural necessity...existence derived its coherence from events having occurred as they occurred, and parties that tried to revise the set record introduced instabilities into that coherence that compounded outward.
THE Primordial Source did not tolerate instabilities.
It didn’t tolerate them as a policy position.
It was incapable of tolerating them the way a material was incapable of tolerating the conditions that caused it to fail.
Osmont had sent him accurate information.
THE Creature looked toward the Relictus.
He sent a short message.
One glance.
The massive ancient being’s attention moved from the Fourth Scale Gilded One it had been occupying itself with and found THE Creature’s position.
It held the look for a moment, the deep awareness behind its gaze taking in whatever THE Creature was communicating through the Entanglement they shared, and then it nodded once.
A single nod.
That was all.
THE Creature sent his reply back through the Entanglement toward THE Youngest, through Infinity and THE Source as the medium, the message traveling the same channel the question had traveled.
’THE Source will know.
Existence will be rectified.’
BOOM!
He sent it and turned back to the engagement without further consideration.
The Devonian Ragnars had reorganized while he’d processed the exchange.

chapters.title: Chapter 5270: Power! I
paragraphs: "Alright," Noah said. "Everything should be taken care of."
Taylor looked at him.
She looked at the surrounding space, which continued doing exactly what it had been doing before he spoke.

The multicolored seas of Infinity moved through the wreckage of the shattered Shelter without urgency. The Ragnar remains sat where they’d been deposited. Nothing had changed, and everything around them reflected that nothing had changed, and yet he’d said everything should be taken care of!
She looked at him again.
"What do you mean taken care of?"The suspicion in her voice was thorough. "Nothing has changed."

"I reached out to someone," Noah said. "They’ll reach out to whatever relevant party exists with a connection to THE Source. They communicated that it will be handled."He looked at the distant space. "So it will be handled."
He didn’t spend a second examining whether that confidence was warranted. THE Creature had sent back eight words through their Entanglement.

That was the exchange in its entirety, and it was enough, because some beings you extended complete trust to not out of naivety but because everything demonstrated across every previous interaction made doubt feel like a waste of attention.
THE Creature had never said a thing he didn’t mean and never meant a thing he didn’t follow through on. The eight words stood.
He looked at Taylor.
"You and Adrastia. Since you were the ones to come forward, we’ll get you back to your respective Observable Existences in due time. I’m a bit busy right now."
Taylor stared at him.
The stare lasted long enough that he counted several Persevere stacks pass through his foundations during it.

"Oh, you’re just a bit busy." She spread her hands wide. "While all of this is happening, and a Gilded Legion is assembling, and there’s a team of time-traveling assassins, and something absurd is clearly occurring in this Observable Existence right now... you are just a bit busy."She dropped her hands.
"Alright. No problem." She crossed her arms. "Could you at least give me your word? Your promise that you’ll keep us alive and get us back where we belong?"
His eyes sharpened.

Something happened in the surrounding weavings of existence the moment she asked. It was low and structural, a resonance moving through the dimensional fabric rather than through the air, the kind of shift that his Source registered before his conscious attention caught up with it.

Whatever Taylor of The Light was underneath her unremarkable presentation and her constant movement and her inability to stop talking, whatever she was at the level his Pillow Talk couldn’t reach... something connected to it was paying attention to this conversation.
He didn’t answer immediately.
Taylor watched the silence stretch and something changed in her face.

"Look." She straightened. Not the nervous straightening she’d done when confirming he hadn’t attacked her. The straightening of someone with something to say. "I know what you are. I know what power you carry. I’ve been talking about it, and existence has been feeding me information about you since I arrived, and none of it is small."
She held his gaze. "But what I’ve learned from ruling an Observable Existence and from everything existence has whispered to me across my entire life..."
She took a breath.

"It doesn’t matter what power an existence carries. I’ve met beings who could split observable existences with nothing but their foundations. I’ve encountered things that made those beings look preliminary. I’ve watched them rise from nothing to something that terrified everything around them, and I’ve heard existence cry."Her rapid eyes held still.

"What those beings had or didn’t have stopped mattering the moment they were gone. What Existence kept carrying forward, what actually persisted in the fabric of existence long after the power dissipated... was their word. Whether they kept it or broke it. Whether the beings they made agreements with could trust those agreements when the moment of truth arrived."
She looked at the consumed Ragnar remains and then back at him.

"You can move through existence as a shitty entity or as a remarkable one. The rankings, the tiers, THE Scales, none of that determines which one you are. The ones who are genuinely outstanding, across every era and every tier I’ve ever heard of, are the ones whose word functions above everything else they are. Power makes you feared. Power makes you capable. Power buys you options." She paused.

"Your word makes you trustworthy. And in the long run, across an existence that spans eons and produces enemies and produces allies and produces every possible category of relationship in between... trustworthy outlasts powerful every single time."
She stopped and ooked at him and waited.
Noah considered her for a moment that had nothing contemplative in it. The decision was already made.
He was simply looking at her before he confirmed it, looking at the being who’d fallen out of a dimensional flicker and talked too much and hadn’t flinched when telling him he could die.
He replied simply.
"I give you my word."
HUUM!
Existence squeezed.

Brief and complete, the space contracting once around the words that had just been spoken and then releasing, the dimensional fabric acknowledging something and ratifying it before returning to its prior state. The resonance he’d felt building from the moment she said promise had found its resolution.
|Verbal agreement entered: Noah Osmont and Taylor of The Light, The Baba Yaga.|
|Terms: Safe conduct and return of Taylor of The Light and Achilles Adrastia to their respective Observable Existences. Agreement witnessed and overseen by THE Primordial Source.|
|Failure to fulfill this agreement will invoke THE Source Curse of Existence upon your foundations. No exceptions.|
He’d expected the notification’s existence. Not entirely its contents.
He looked at the woman near him.
"THE Baba Yaga."He let the designation sit. "Why are you classified that way?"
Taylor’s eyes went wide. It was the mortified expression of someone who’d hoped a particular piece of personal data would remain unmentioned and had discovered it would not.
"I’m actually a very nice person." She said this immediately.

"Every now and then, whenever I’m seriously wronged, I tend to go a little crazy, and I got that distinction carved into Vakochev’s Scales during one of my crazy times."She pointed at him. "Don’t pay attention to it. It’s not representative! I am actually a very nice person and I have many people who would confirm this!"
She said the last sentence like she needed it on the record specifically.
Noah nodded once and waved his hand in the direction away from him.
Taylor looked at his hand. Looked at him. Looked at his hand again.

"Are you shooing me away?"Her voice climbed half a register. "Where are your social skills? Who does that? You just made a formal agreement, overseen by THE Primordial Source, no less, with a ruler of a lower Observable Existence, who has personally convinced Gilded Ones to leave her and her entire Observable Existence alone by the way, and your response is to shoo her away?"
She stepped toward him instead of away.

"You could build a connection here. Expand your Entanglements. Do you know how you make yourself genuinely unkillable in existence? Not power. Power has ceilings. Connections don’t. The more beings across existence who are invested in your survival, the harder you become to erase from it. And I," she said, with the emphasis of someone who considered this their strongest argument, "am a very interesting person with a very unusual ability and a very broad network of existences who owe me favors."
She looked at the surrounding wreckage and the continuous flames burning through his form. "For you to be shooing me away, just what exactly is happening here that you’re so busy with?"

chapters.title: Chapter 5271: Power! II
paragraphs: Her eyes were deeply suspicious and moving fast.
BOOM!
And at such a time...
An aurora cut across all of Observable Existence.

Multicolored brilliance, immediate and vast, light shining with Infinity and budding Cause expressions that had no single origin point in the surrounding space... the light came from somewhere deeper, from something in the process of becoming rather than something that had already arrived. It spread across Observable Existence from horizon to horizon without gradient!
Noah’s eyes went to it.

|THE Infiniverse’s transformation is entering critical phase. THE Infinite Cause is building toward full emergence as continuous applications of Persevere from THE Primordial Tongue accelerated foundational development beyond projections. The Calabi-Yau Foldings were unable to fully contain the emergence-light. THE Aurora of Existential Causality is leaking through at the boundary layers. The concealment remains functional, but the aurora is visible to any existence in Observable Existence with Cause sensitivity.|

He’d hoped for silence. Silence had always been optimistic. An Observable Existence emerging from a previously concealed domain was an event of sufficient magnitude that concealment had a physical ceiling, and that ceiling had been reached!
He managed what could be managed. The rest was what it was.
Beside him, Taylor had gone completely still.
Her rapid eyes stopped moving.

She looked at the aurora spreading across the full visible expanse of Observable Existence, the multicolored light washing over the wreckage of the Shelter, and her face cycled through several expressions in quick succession before landing on one that was pure unguarded excitement.
"Holy shit." Her voice was low. "Existence is telling me this is the Aurora of Existential Causality."She turned to him.
"Something like that only blooms when an Observable Existence is actually emerging. Why would..." She turned back to the aurora. Then to him. The excitement intensified!

"Hey. Hey, don’t you dare go anywhere!" She moved toward him. "I love interesting things about existence more than anything else in any existence I have ever been in. Just tell me. What is happening here? What do you have going on?! Please!"
She floated toward him with the clear intention of attaching herself to his vicinity if it became necessary!
BOOM!
And at such a point, once more...
Existence cracked.

Countless light years away, at multiple points simultaneously, the dimensional fabric of Observable Existence split- large splits, clean splits, the kind that Legion-class vessels produced when navigating from THE Braneworld into the space below.
The golden entry signatures of the Gilded Ones bloomed!
Taylor looked at the entry signatures.

"Oh." Her voice dropped back to conversational. "The Legion coming for you has also arrived. My main body is with them. Adrastia too." She looked at the entry signatures and then at the aurora and then at Noah.

"This is turning into a significant mess. You have something absurd happening here, and something monstrous is arriving from outside, and...." She looked around the immediate space. "Is everything about to go badly?"
She paused.

"But you said it was handled. With complete confidence." She looked around them slowly."I don’t sense any additional changes nearby. If nothing comes of your outreach to THE Source, you’re going to be facing that entire Legion alone."
Noah wasn’t attending to the last part.
His attention was on the aurora of THE Infiniverse’s emergence, on the entry signatures of the Legion, on the continuous Persevere stacking moving through his foundations every second!
He trusted THE Creature’s word the way he trusted the ground to be solid. Because THE Creature had never once given him a reason to doubt!
He waited.
HUUUM!
His eyes opened wide.
Beside him, Taylor went silent for the first time since her arrival without being told to.
Both of them looked up and across the vast distance of Observable Existence at the same moment, drawn by the same shift...not sound, not light, not any sensory input in the ordinary sense!

A change in the pressure of the space itself, the arrival of something that rewrote the ambient conditions of Observable Existence the way the presence of a very large mass rewrote the behavior of everything near it.
The aura came before the being resolved visually.

Invisible flames that Noah’s Source recognized at the foundational level... THE Primordial Source, not accessed, not cultivated toward, but carried, present in the being’s existence the way Infinity was present in his, as a component of what the being was rather than a capability it had developed.
Their body was born...from THE Primordial Source!
The aura spread across Gigaparsecs between the being’s position and Noah’s and covered the distance as though distance was a secondary consideration.
Then the being itself resolved.
Titanic. Humanoid.An obsidian stellar suit fitted to a frame that wore it with the ease of something that had been clothed in significance long enough that the clothing had become natural.
White shirt beneath the jacket. A tie in obsidian that matched the suit and sat without adjustment against the white shirt’s surface!

Sleek dark hair. Radiant fair skin. At his side, in a resting grip that communicated preparedness without aggression, an obsidian sheath, and within the sheath, a blade burning with concentrations of THE Primordial Source that made everything quiver!
He was Gigaparsecs away.
He felt immediate.

His head turned and found Noah across the distance with the directness of something that had been given coordinates and had confirmed them at a glance. He observed the aurora spreading across Observable Existence. He paused and turned to find Taylor, who had relocated herself behind Noah’s Primus Apeiron form.
He looked at her. He registered her. He then turned to the Gilded Legion’s signatures spreading through Observable Existence, the vessels moving into formation!
And...
And...!
His voice came through Observable Existence with the unhurried precision of someone who chose every word and delivered every syllable at its exact weight.
"Manners."
HUUM!
"Maketh."
WAA!
"Man."
Obsidian brilliance spread outward from his position.

It...was not an attack. It was condition- the brilliance establishing itself through Observable Existence the way a fundamental rule established itself, present everywhere within its reach at once, operative without requiring anything to accept it.
Noah recognized it for he had began doing something similar to it.
|Observable Existence: Lockdown active.|

|All existences at THE Fourth Scale or below are unable to enter or exit this Observable Existence. The lockdown applies without exception and will remain in effect until the originating authority rescinds it.|
An entity of unfathomable wonders had made his descent while THE Infiniverse was taking a quintessential step forward!
